title: Use bash for bin/setup
body:
That the ruby version is mostly shelling out is a hint that a shell language might be a better choice. It's more direct, slightly faster, it sidesteps chicken/egg problems when installing ruby, and writing things in bash is fun.

It's good to have an excuse to flex those shell muscles 💪

Some different opinions here, where @jorgemanrubia posted about converting in the opposite direction: https://x.com/jorgemanru/status/1808405894889169124. I think the purpose of the script matters: a ruby script that installs a specific ruby version, as our `setup` is wont to do, can be fraught! When we're bootstrapping the system, staying close to the metal is an advantage. For scripts that depend on a functioning environment, ruby is the way to go.

Release notes

Sourced from rexml's releases.

REXML 3.3.6 - 2024-08-22

Improvements

  • Removed duplicated entity expansions for performance.

    • GH-194
    • Patch by Viktor Ivarsson.

  • Improved namespace conflicted attribute check performance. It was too slow for deep elements.

    • Reported by l33thaxor.

Fixes

  • Fixed a bug that default entity expansions are counted for security check. Default entity expansions should not be counted because they don't have a security risk.

    • GH-198
    • GH-199
    • Patch Viktor Ivarsson

  • Fixed a parser bug that parameter entity references in internal subsets are expanded. It's not allowed in the XML specification.

    • GH-191
    • Patch by NAITOH Jun.

  • Fixed a stream parser bug that user-defined entity references in text aren't expanded.

    • GH-200
    • Patch by NAITOH Jun.

Thanks

  • l33thaxor

6.4.3

title: Bump sqlite3 from 2.0.4 to 2.1.0
body:
Bumps [sqlite3](https://github.com/sparklemotion/sqlite3-ruby) from 2.0.4 to 2.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from sqlite3's releases.

2.1.0 / 2024-09-24

Ruby

  • This release drops support for Ruby 3.0. #563 @​flavorjones

Fork safety improvements

Sqlite itself is not fork-safe. Specifically, writing in a child process to a database connection that was created in the parent process may corrupt the database file. To mitigate this risk, sqlite3-ruby has implemented the following changes:

  • All open writable database connections carried across a fork() will immediately be closed in the child process to mitigate the risk of corrupting the database file.
  • These connections will be incompletely closed ("discarded") which will result in a one-time memory leak in the child process.

If it's at all possible, we strongly recommend that you close writable database connections in the parent before forking. If absolutely necessary (and you know what you're doing), you may suppress the fork safety warnings by calling SQLite3::ForkSafety.suppress_warnings!.

See the README's "Fork Safety" section and adr/2024-09-fork-safety.md for more information. [#558, #565, #566] @​flavorjones

Improved

  • Use sqlite3_close_v2 to close databases in a deferred manner if there are unclosed prepared statements. Previously closing a database while statements were open resulted in a BusyException. See https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/close.html for more context. #557 @​flavorjones
  • When setting a Database busy_handler, fire the write barrier to prevent potential crashes during the GC mark phase. #556 @​jhawthorn

Documentation

  • The FAQ.md has been updated to fix some inaccuracies. #562 @​rickhull

New Contributors

  • @​rickhull made their first contribution in sparklemotion/sqlite3-ruby#562

Changelog

Sourced from sqlite3's changelog.

2.1.0 / 2024-09-24

Ruby

  • This release drops support for Ruby 3.0. #563 @​flavorjones

Fork safety improvements

Sqlite itself is not fork-safe. Specifically, writing in a child process to a database connection that was created in the parent process may corrupt the database file. To mitigate this risk, sqlite3-ruby has implemented the following changes:

  • All open writable database connections carried across a fork() will immediately be closed in the child process to mitigate the risk of corrupting the database file.
  • These connections will be incompletely closed ("discarded") which will result in a one-time memory leak in the child process.

If it's at all possible, we strongly recommend that you close writable database connections in the parent before forking. If absolutely necessary (and you know what you're doing), you may suppress the fork safety warnings by calling SQLite3::ForkSafety.suppress_warnings!.

See the README's "Fork Safety" section and adr/2024-09-fork-safety.md for more information. [#558, #565, #566] @​flavorjones

Improved

  • Use sqlite3_close_v2 to close databases in a deferred manner if there are unclosed prepared statements. Previously closing a database while statements were open resulted in a BusyException. See https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/close.html for more context. #557 @​flavorjones
  • When setting a Database busy_handler, fire the write barrier to prevent potential crashes during the GC mark phase. #556 @​jhawthorn

Documentation

  • The FAQ.md has been updated to fix some inaccuracies. #562 @​rickhull

title: Unnest bubbles index
body:
This PR unnests the bubbles index from the buckets namespace and makes it possible to save filters that cut across multiple buckets.

To do this, we've added a `bucketable` delegated type to `Bucket`. `Bucketables` can be a `Project` or a `Filter`; where `Filters` are a collection of URL query params like `?assignments=773523953&bucket_ids=693169840&indexed_by=most_discussed&tag_ids=1014178784`.

Using delegated types makes it easy to query, paginate, sort, and cache `Project` and `Filter` records side-by-side for indexing on the main page as follows:

![CleanShot 2024-11-04 at 00 14 06](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6894189-07f5-4f13-842f-f9d2f8b5570f)

Users can manually input their own collection of filters to be saved as `Filter` bucketables. In the end, they'll just be querying the `/bubbles` endpoint with different query params — as persisted or manually inputted.

Finally, navigating to a bucket will now hit the `/bubbles` index with a single query param: `?bucket_ids=:bucket_id`.

To-do
- [x] Caching considerations
- [ ] Testing
- [ ] Clean up

title: Unnest bubble filters
body:
Coming from https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/pull/129

This is a simplified version of that PR, where we're reworking persisted filters to cut across multiple buckets — but we're listing filters separate to buckets in the main bucket index page.

Not having to list them together means we can use two different models. This might make paginating tricky, but it's too early to know what we want there. So we're taking smaller steps towards what we do know we want — and that's filtering all bubbles across all accessible buckets.

title: Use counter cache to track bubble comments
body:
* Counter caches don't use `COUNT` statements — they increment/decrement counters by 1 https://github.com/basecamp/rails/blob/59064f88d8abda19f81d4bf400cd17d91eb9c65c/activerecord/lib/active_record/associations/belongs_to_association.rb#L53-L59
* Which means introducing a condition is a matter of asking the incumbent record whether it should be counted, not a matter of introducing a `WHERE` clause
* The counter is updated using `update_all` — no callbacks are run https://github.com/basecamp/rails/blob/f1cc2221315b82989f37c999da6e8ba0d0e270eb/activerecord/lib/active_record/relation.rb#L943
* But the bubble _will_ be touched if the association is configured to do so https://github.com/basecamp/rails/blob/59064f88d8abda19f81d4bf400cd17d91eb9c65c/activerecord/lib/active_record/associations/belongs_to_association.rb#L106
* Additionally, dirty-tracked changes on the counter column are cleared after incrementing/decrementing and touching https://github.com/basecamp/rails/blob/3ae6284f0e4f252429210e469b2129a84495612e/activerecord/lib/active_record/persistence.rb#L648
* That means if we went down this path we have three options to recalculate an activity score after a comment is added
   1) hook into `after_touch` (suboptimal, since most touching doesn't require updating the activity score, and no dirty attribute tracking is available to do it conditionally)
   2) hook into `clear_comments_count_change` (hacky, this isn't what the method is for — it's meant for clearing dirty attribute changes, which unfortunately there are none at this point, since `comments_count_will_change!` is never called)
   3) use the counter cache for counting — but recalculate activity in a `Comment` callback (which would have to be `after_commit` because the Comment's `after_save` happens before the counter cache change)

I'm making this PR and then closing to document my findings. But I don't think this is the way to go. I'm thinking we should increment/decrement the counter manually, as well as instruct the bubble to recalculate its score — all in one go inside a Comment's `after_save` callback. Like this:

```diff
diff --git a/app/models/bubble.rb b/app/models/bubble.rb
index a52cb6b..2711997 100644
--- a/app/models/bubble.rb
+++ b/app/models/bubble.rb
@@ -38,6 +38,12 @@ def activity_count
     boost_count + messages.comments.size
   end

+  def rescore
+    update! \
+      activity_count: boost_count + comments_count, # for sorting by activity
+      expires_at: 1.month.from_now # for popping due to entropy
+  end
+
   private
     def set_default_title
       self.title = title.presence || "Untitled"
diff --git a/app/models/bubble/boostable.rb b/app/models/bubble/boostable.rb
index 0853603..f4b1792 100644
--- a/app/models/bubble/boostable.rb
+++ b/app/models/bubble/boostable.rb
@@ -9,6 +9,7 @@ def boost!
     transaction do
       increment! :boost_count
       track_event :boosted
+      rescore
     end
   end
 end
diff --git a/app/models/comment.rb b/app/models/comment.rb
index 4a9afb2..86b235d 100644
--- a/app/models/comment.rb
+++ b/app/models/comment.rb
@@ -4,4 +4,20 @@ class Comment < ApplicationRecord
   belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

   searchable_by :body, using: :comments_search_index
+
+  after_create :increment_bubble_comments_count, :rescore_bubble
+  after_destroy :decrement_bubble_comments_count, :rescore_bubble
+
+  private
+    def increment_bubble_comments_count
+      message.bubble.increment!(:comments_count)
+    end
+
+    def decrement_bubble_comments_count
+      message.bubble.decrement!(:comments_count)
+    end
+
+    def rescore_bubble
+      message.bubble.rescore
+    end
 end
```

title: Bump sqlite3 from 2.1.0 to 2.3.0
body:
Bumps [sqlite3](https://github.com/sparklemotion/sqlite3-ruby) from 2.1.0 to 2.3.0.
Release notes

Sourced from sqlite3's releases.

2.3.0 / 2024-11-20

Added

  • The SQLITE_DBPAGE extension is now enabled by default, which implements an eponymous-only virtual table that provides direct access to the underlying database file by interacting with the pager. See https://www.sqlite.org/dbpage.html for more information. #578 @​flavorjones
  • The DBSTAT extension is now enabled by default, which implements a read-only eponymous virtual table that returns information about the amount of disk space used to store the content of an SQLite database. See https://sqlite.org/dbstat.html for more information. #580 @​pawurb @​flavorjones
  • Database#optimize which wraps the pragma optimize; statement. Also added Constants::Optimize to allow advanced users to pass a bitmask of options. See https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html#pragma_optimize. #572 @​alexcwatt @​flavorjones
  • SQLite3::VERSION_INFO contains a bag of metadata about the gem and the sqlite library used. SQLite3::SQLITE_PACKAGED_LIBRARIES and SQLite3::SQLITE_PRECOMPILED_LIBRARIES indicate how the gem was built. #581 @​flavorjones

Fixed

title: Wire up comboboxes
body:
This PR adds my `HotwireCombobox` gem so we can wire up all comboboxes in the bubble perma.

@jzimdars some notes about styling:

* The main way I designed the component to be styled is via BEM CSS classes. Since you're an expert, I'd suggest inspecting the markup via devtools and overriding the [default styles](https://github.com/josefarias/hotwire_combobox/blob/main/app/assets/stylesheets/hotwire_combobox.css) as needed. But there's minimal documentation about styling at https://hotwirecombobox.com, too.
* The secondary way is by customizing each element. The combobox is composed of many elements (a main wrapper, an input, a listbox, a dialog which is only shown on mobile, and many more) so the way to customize each element with attributes (including `class` but also `data-` attrs, etc), is by passing a block to the combobox. I'm thinking you might want to pass classes this way.
  *  I've implemented this by overriding the gem's main `combobox_tag` helper — so that the options apply to all comboboxes.
  * [Here](https://github.com/josefarias/hotwire_combobox/blob/main/test/dummy/app/views/comboboxes/custom_attrs.html.erb) are all the available customizations, if needed.
* Finally, please let me know if there are ways to make things easier for you to manipulate. I'm totally open to not using the gem if it's too hard — but I have a strong suspicion whatever changes in ergonomics we need to make will be easier and faster than not using the gem.

title: Use House for MD comments
body:
|**composing**|**rendered**|
|-|-|
|![CleanShot 2024-11-29 at 18 44 13](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c314c328-5a33-4c78-9347-b1476b963f01)|![CleanShot 2024-11-29 at 18 45 38](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa3a5921-d8bf-4465-80b6-51641efb2871)|


Deviations from other House implementations:
- Uploads are associated to the account, instead of the markdown record
  - Fizzy's markdown records don't exist as you're composing them (e.g. for new comments), contrary to Writebook
- Added a plaintext renderer (for searching content)
  - Added convenience methods for `#{name}_html` and `#{name}_plain_text`
- Markdown is sanitized, since it's no longer necessarily trusted
- Removed embeds for now
  - Wasn't causing any issues, we just don't need it (yet)
-  Fixed a bug with `slug_url`'s default params
- Some refactoring around specifying and calling a markdown renderer (to make it agnostic to the renderer's interface — previously it had to respond to `#render`), and refactored our bespoke `MarkdownRenderer` class

title: Bump rails-html-sanitizer from 1.6.0 to 1.6.1
body:
Bumps [rails-html-sanitizer](https://github.com/rails/rails-html-sanitizer) from 1.6.0 to 1.6.1.
Release notes

Sourced from rails-html-sanitizer's releases.

1.6.1 / 2024-12-02

This is a performance and security release which addresses several possible XSS vulnerabilities.

  • The dependency on Nokogiri is updated to v1.15.7 or >=1.16.8.

    This change addresses CVE-2024-53985 (https://github.com/rails/rails-html-sanitizer/security/advisories/GHSA-w8gc-x259-rc7x).

    Mike Dalessio

  • Disallowed tags will be pruned when they appear in foreign content (i.e. SVG or MathML content), regardless of the prune: option value. Previously, disallowed tags were "stripped" unless the gem was configured with the prune: true option.

    The CVEs addressed by this change are:

    • CVE-2024-53986 (https://github.com/rails/rails-html-sanitizer/security/advisories/GHSA-638j-pmjw-jq48)
    • CVE-2024-53987 (https://github.com/rails/rails-html-sanitizer/security/advisories/GHSA-2x5m-9ch4-qgrr)

    Mike Dalessio

  • The tags "noscript", "mglyph", and "malignmark" will not be allowed, even if explicitly added to the allowlist. If applications try to allow any of these tags, a warning is emitted and the tags are removed from the allow-list.

    The CVEs addressed by this change are:

    • CVE-2024-53988 (https://github.com/rails/rails-html-sanitizer/security/advisories/GHSA-cfjx-w229-hgx5)
    • CVE-2024-53989 (https://github.com/rails/rails-html-sanitizer/security/advisories/GHSA-rxv5-gxqc-xx8g)

    Please note that we may restore support for allowing "noscript" in a future release. We do not expect to ever allow "mglyph" or "malignmark", though, especially since browser support is minimal for these tags.

    Mike Dalessio

  • Improve performance by eliminating needless operations on attributes that are being removed. #188

    Mike Dalessio

title: Implement all-access buckets
body:
This PR wires up the "everyone" switch in the bucket settings page.

We don't anticipate we'll need further access control. So I went with a simple `all_access` bool on the buckets table.

The PR takes care of granting access when changing a bucket to be `all_access`, as well as when a new user is created. We're also ensuring the bucket is visible to `Current.user` in `BucketScoped`.

Finally, I've removed some unused code from earlier iterations.

Ref. https://3.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/37331921/todos/7973209059

title: Introduce tenanting
body:
## User-facing changes

- http://default.fizzy.localhost:3006 is where the seed data can be found
- http://fizzy.localhost:3006 will start the "first run" signup flow, which now has a subdomain field

## Kicking the tires on this branch

- rebuild the database: `bin/rails db:drop db:prepare db:seed`
- `bin/rails bin/dev`
- browse to http://default.fizzy.localhost:3006 to develop as normal with seed data
- browse to http://fizzy.localhost:3006 to go through first run signup

## Implementation details

This PR does a few notable things to implement a tenanted sqlite3 database for Fizzy:

1. Introduce a `Tenant` model in a non-tenanted secondary database
2. Tenant the ApplicationRecord models using https://github.com/basecamp/active_record-tenanted
3. Introduce middleware for selecting the tenant based on subdomain
4. Extend the "first run" flow to include a subdomain field, and the controller creates both a new `Tenant` and, in it, the new `Account`
5. Modify `TestCase` to handle parallel testing and creating the "fixture" tenant and its database, and modify `IntegrationTest` so the host used is the fixture tenant

## Design decisions

Some design decisions which I made along the way (which are totally changeable):

*1. Tenanting with a subdomain (instead of a URL path component)*

I chose this because the implementation was simple and therefore would get us to a conversation about it fastest.

Note that the "first run" flow must be on the apex domain. (E.g., if the tenant will be live at "foobar.fizzy.biz" then the first-run flow happens at "fizzy.biz".)

On the downside, the first-run flow ends with a redirect to the subdomain. For now, the user will need to re-login at that point, but we can make this seamless with a bit more effort if it's the flow we decide we want.


*2. The "slug" used for subdomain is separate from the database name (instead of using the same ID for both)*

This leaves the door open to allowing users to change their subdomain/slug.

Related, `Tenant` generates a permanent SecureRandom string for the database file name.

title: Introduce tenanting (attempt 2)
body:
This is a second attempt to land tenanting, and is a bit different from the first PR at #159.

Significant changes from that PR:

- First run sign-in flow actually works!
- There is no "Tenant" Active Record model. Instead, `Tenant` is a PORO which inherits its behavior from the gem (but can be overridden in the app).
- Tenanted databases are configured to be in a subdirectory:
  ```
  storage/test
  ├── test-tenant-0
  │   └── main.sqlite3
  ├── test-tenant-1
  │   └── main.sqlite3
  │ ...
  ```
- the private gem is configured to be bundled into the Dockerfile correctly
- bin/setup calls db:seed (which isn't run by db:prepare for tenanted database (yet))
- the TenantSelector middleware lives entirely in the gem, not the app
- Dev and test environments set up a default "current tenant" to avoid having to set it repeatedly and explicitly in the console.

As a result, the changes needed to tenant-ize the application are very small, see cc6f80c1.

One wart that I'm not happy with (but can't figure out how to work around) is the use of a "protoshard", which is a fully-migrated, empty, readonly instance of the tenanted database. This is necessary because Rails needs to query a live database to resolve attribute metadata. The gem makes this protoshard the current tenant in "untenanted" contexts to prevent Rails from raising exceptions in "untenanted" contexts.

One example of what I mean: The "first run" controller must be untenanted, because part of its job is to create a new tenant. The form template calls `User.new`. If User attributes/columns have not yet been loaded by rails, then [this Rails code](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/activerecord/lib/active_record/inheritance.rb#L61) will try to access the database. If the current shard is `nil` then the gem will correctly raise a `NoCurrentTenant` exception. Setting the current shard to the protoshard instead of `nil` allows Rails's implicit lazy loading to continue to work.

The gem itself needs some tests to be backfilled, and needs documentation; but if you want to take a look it's on this branch: https://github.com/basecamp/active_record-tenanted/tree/flavorjones-more-magic-please

title: Implement bubbles divider
body:
Two major components to this: dragging of the divider and persisting its position.

Dragging makes use of the browser's drag and drop API.

Persisting is interesting because it expands on our filter model, which we're still refining.

One question is where do we persist the position? These dividers show up in three contexts:

* Viewing a single bucket's bubbles
* Viewing a persisted filter
* Viewing a non-persisted filter (i.e. starting from a single bucket's bubbles and refining the filter without saving it)

For now, I've opted for persisting it on the bucket as a db column, and on filters inside the "fields" hash — which also contains "indexed_by", "terms", and "assignment_status".

This opens up an interesting door regarding filters. Consider the fact that you're able to save a filter to your home screen, then go view a single bucket's bubbles, and refine its filters until you replicate the same filter you've saved. Then, you click on the "Save to home" button. What happens then?

Previously, we've hashed and persisted JSON representations of filters, so we can enforce a uniqueness constraint based on that and avoid duplicate filters that way. But persisting the divider position as part of the filter complicates that because you can create two filters that are _essentially_ the same, except for the divider's position, and then save both.

We don't want that scenario to create a duplicate filter. So, similar to an email's essence digest in HEY, we only hash _essential params_ (_essential_ as in _essence_)— and enforce uniqueness based on _that_.

We're treading a fine line between flexibility and complexity here. I think filters are more useful than they are complex, even today, when we haven't finished refining them. But they're certainly quite clever. So we should keep an eye on this complexity as we keep building. In the end, I think they're turning up to be quite a central part of Fizzy. So we wanna make them powerful, as well as easy to work with.

title: Simplify filters
body:
1. Implement `Filter.from_params` factory, which will take a collection of params and return the matching saved filter, or build a new unpersisted filter if none exist. This will give us a reference filter id for use in caching and subsequent requests for `PATCH`ing or `DELETE`ing the filter, etc.
2. Implement `Filter.normalize_params` to encapsulate logic behind cleaning up a `Hash` or `ActionController::Parameters` instance for hashing, for the purposes of ensuring uniqueness and looking up filters by "essence"
3. Implement `Filter.find_by_params`, which knows how to find filters by said "essence"
4. Remove `Filter#to_params`. We get all we need from `Filter#as_params`, which returns a `Hash` representation of a `Filter`. `to_params` previously converted `as_params` into a `ActionController::Parameters` instance. We don't need to do that. Having a single method removes ambiguity regarding which one to use.
5. Rename `Filter#assignments` to `Filter#assignment_status`, which better communicates its intention of persisting whether we're filtering "unassigned" bubbles.
6. Other minor naming and testing improvements

cc @kevinmcconnell

title: Fix divider drag jankiness
body:
[Screencast From 2025-01-16 12-18-34.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2515f19c-c874-47b9-b609-640446708aba)

When bubble rows have tags at the bottom, we can get some jitter when the mouse sits at just the right spot while dragging the divider. I'm not entirely sure yet why this doesn't happen when there are no tags. But this change makes sure we don't move the divider unless there's enough overlap while dragging.

It also turns off hover styles while dragging.

title: Create before draft
body:
This improves the "new bubble" flow, but introducing a new `creating` status for bubbles that are still being populated. Once you're ready to "save" your bubble, you can choose to publish it, or save it as a draft. In either case the bubble will then be visible to you; if it's published it will also be visible to others.

If you abandon a `creating` bubble, it won't show up in the normal views. It will be as if it was never created. However, if you return to the New Bubble view shortly after abandoning one, we'll offer to restore it for you, in case you left it accidentally (or your computer crashed, whatever). We'll garbage-collect abandoned bubbles after some time elapses.

Still remaining to do:

- [x] Surface the recently abandoned bubbles
- [x] Garbage collect
- [x] Auto-save the bubble title, so edits are not lost when accessing other parts of the form
- [ ] Separate the comment section from the main form
- [ ] Submit comment field when submitting form
- [ ] Style the new controls (publish buttons, etc)

title: Bump net-imap from 0.5.5 to 0.5.6
body:
Bumps [net-imap](https://github.com/ruby/net-imap) from 0.5.5 to 0.5.6.
Release notes

Sourced from net-imap's releases.

v0.5.6

What's Changed

🔒 Security Fix

Fixes CVE-2025-25186 (GHSA-7fc5-f82f-cx69): A malicious server can exhaust client memory by sending APPENDUID or COPYUID responses with very large uid-set ranges. Net::IMAP::UIDPlusData expands these ranges into arrays of integers.

Fix with minor API changes

Set config.parser_use_deprecated_uidplus_data to false to replace UIDPlusData with AppendUIDData and CopyUIDData. These classes store their UIDs as Net::IMAP::SequenceSet objects (not expanded into arrays of integers). Code that does not handle APPENDUID or COPYUID responses should not see any difference. Code that does handle these responses may need to be updated.

For v0.3.8, this option is not available For v0.4.19, the default value is true. For v0.5.6, the default value is :up_to_max_size. For v0.6.0, the only allowed value will be false (UIDPlusData will be removed from v0.6).

Mitigate with backward compatible API

Adjust config.parser_max_deprecated_uidplus_data_size to limit the maximum UIDPlusData UID set size. When config.parser_use_deprecated_uidplus_data == true, larger sets will crash. When config.parser_use_deprecated_uidplus_data == :up_to_max_size, larger sets will use AppendUIDData or CopyUIDData.

For v0.3,8, this limit is hard-coded to 10,000. For v0.4.19, this limit defaults to 1000. For v0.5.6, this limit defaults to 100. For v0.6.0, the only allowed value will be 0 (UIDPlusData will be removed from v0.6).

Please Note: unhandled responses

If the client does not add response handlers to prune unhandled responses, a malicious server can still eventually exhaust all client memory, by repeatedly sending malicious responses. However, net-imap has always retained unhandled responses, and it has always been necessary for long-lived connections to prune these responses. This is not significantly different from connecting to a trusted server with a long-lived connection. To limit the maximum number of retained responses, a simple handler might look something like the following:

limit = 1000
imap.add_response_handler do |resp|
  next unless resp.respond_to?(:name) && resp.respond_to?(:data)
  name = resp.name
  code = resp.data.code&.name if resp.data.is_a?(Net::IMAP::ResponseText)
  imap.responses(name) { _1.slice!(0...-limit) }
  imap.responses(code) { _1.slice!(0...-limit) }
end

  • ✨ Add SequenceSet methods for querying about duplicates by @​nevans in ruby/net-imap#384

  • ✨ Add SequenceSet#ordered_at by @​nevans in ruby/net-imap#397
  • ✨ Add AppendUIDData and CopyUIDData classes by @​nevans in ruby/net-imap#400
  • 🔧 Add parser config for APPENDUID/COPYUID, 🗑️ Deprecate UIDPlusData by @​nevans in ruby/net-imap#401

Fixed

  • 🐛 Fix SequenceSet merging in another SequenceSet by @​nevans in ruby/net-imap#377
  • 🐛 Fix SequenceSet count dups with multiple "*" by @​nevans in ruby/net-imap#387

Changelog

Sourced from rack's changelog.

Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. For info on how to format all future additions to this file please reference Keep A Changelog.

Unreleased

Added

  • Introduce Rack::VERSION constant. (#2199, [@​ioquatix])
  • ISO-2022-JP encoded parts within MIME Multipart sections of an HTTP request body will now be converted to UTF-8. (#2245, [@​nappa])

Changed

  • Invalid cookie keys will now raise an error. (#2193, [@​ioquatix])
  • Rack::MediaType#params now handles empty strings. (#2229, [@​jeremyevans])

Deprecated

  • Rack::Auth::AbstractRequest#request is deprecated without replacement. (#2229, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Rack::Request#parse_multipart (private method designed to be overridden in subclasses) is deprecated without replacement. (#2229, [@​jeremyevans])

Removed

  • Rack::Request#values_at is removed. (#2200, [@​ioquatix])
  • Rack::Logger is removed with no replacement. (#2196, [@​ioquatix])
  • Automatic cache invalidation in Rack::Request#{GET,POST} has been removed. (#2230, [@​jeremyevans])

Fixed

  • Rack::RewindableInput::Middleware no longer wraps a nil input. (#2259, @​tt)

title: Notification preferences
body:
This allows people to customize their notification preferences, as follows:

- Adds a "watching" property on each bubble. By default, you'll be watching bubbles that you create, are assigned to, or have commented on. You'll get notifications of changes to bubbles that you're watching.
- You can also toggle the "watching" property on or off manually, so you can opt in or out to the notifications on a bubble-by-bubble basis.
- Future activity can opt you back in. So if you turn off watching for a bubble but then you comment on it, you'll automatically be watching it again. (But you can always turn it off again, if you really want to.)
- Additionally, you can subscribe to a bucket. Subscribing to a bucket also enables notifications for all the activity in that bucket -- except for the cases where you've explicitly opted-out by un-watching a bubble. In other words, the bubble's watch status has precedence over the bucket subscription.

## FYI

- The `Subscription` model is polymorphic because we've discussed making other things subscribable, like tags. If we end up not doing that, we can simplify this to a regular association.
- `Subscription` and `Watch` are quite similar, but they differ in that a `Watch` can be explicitly "off". Depending on where we land with the choices we expose here, we might end up folding these into a single class, But for now I think they're subtly different enough to both exist. We'll see!

@jzimdars

title: Autosave comments
body:
This PR does two things:

1. It introduces an autosave controller that automatically saves unposted comment content to `localStorage` if you navigate away or reload the page and restores it when you return to keep you from losing your work. It's based on Basecamp's same behavior in that there is nothing user-facing for this, it just happens automatically.
2. It applies the same autosave behavior to the special first-comment field used when creating or editing a drafted bubble. This fixes a bug @uptonic reported where `remote-auto-save` loses markdown formatting when it saves to the server. This is the part I'd most like your feedback on, @kevinmcconnell. Maybe this `autosave` makes `remote-auto-save` unnecessary. Right now they work in tandem (which might be fine, too).

Here's demo of the bug Scott reported:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31948c7d-24a2-4a4d-8b29-e91dd2091b3d

title: Introduce tenanting (v3)
body:
After discussions in January, the complex first run controller that allowed users to create a new tenant has been dropped, and I've left the "first run" controller as-is.

New tenants must be created by a developer, but this is easy enough to do from the console:

```
ApplicationRecord.create_tenant("foo")
```

and then when a user visits the tenant subdomain for the first time, they'll be greeted with the same "first run" experience we already have, to create the first user for the tenant.

For the development experience, a tenant named `development-tenant` is created by default by `bin/setup` or `rails db:prepare`, and you'll visit:

> http://development-tenant.fizzy.locahost:3006

title: More dynamic activity scores
body:
This introduces a more dynamic system of activity scoring, to improve the way bubbles "bubble up" due to their activity. There are a few different parts we can tune here, and it's likely we'll need to make adjustments once we get a feel for how this works in practice.

The basic idea here is:

- We assign points for certain types of event that happen on a bubble. A boost gets 1 point, a comment gets 10 points, and so on.
- These points decay over time, at a rate of 50% per day. So old activity is worth much less than new activity. Bubbles should rise up quickly when acted upon, bit will float back down if left idle.
- Some comments can score higher than others: the first comment from each person on a bubble is worth more (20) because it signals that more people are getting involved; and comments that follow a comment by a different author are also worth more (15) because that signals there's ongoing conversation between people, not just a series of notes being left by one individual.

In terms of implementation, we persist the score on the bubble whenever it changes, but we handle the decay on the client side. That allows us to cache the bubble representation without having to continually change it while its activity decays.

We also keep a separate `activity_score_order` attribute on the model. This can be used to sort the bubbles in order of "most active", without having to think about the decay.

title: Migration script for make Fizzy multi-tenant
body:
ref: https://3.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/39446225/documents/8399474398

The script takes advantage of the fact that we can bind to the existing untenanted database by adding it explicitly (and temporarily) as a readonly shard to the `database.yml`, and so in the script `while_untenanted` is connected to the original database.

storage/tenants/%{tenant}/ is now the root directory for all state stored for a particular tenant, including active storage and the database.

We leave the existing files and production database in place after the migration, in case we need to roll back (by reverting the code and config).

We also don't do a granular active storage blob copy, since the attachments are mostly on Account (and not on Bubble). Instead we hardlink the blobs on disk (so we don't take up additional space with duplicates).

Finally, we're manually adding the kamal-proxy hosts to the deploy file, so that we can generate letsencrypt certs for the subdomains. This is only intended to be a short-term solution, we'll want something like a wildcard cert before we go live.

title: New visual design
Quieter notifs
body:
@jzimdars I think this gets the notifications closer to what we need:

- If you're subscribed to a collection, you'll get notified when a new ticket is published in that collection.
- If you're watching a ticket, you'll get notified about all activity on that ticket.

To be watching a ticket you have to either have been involved in it (you get assigned, you comment, you created it, etc); or you can manually enable the notification bell for that ticket. But simply being subscribed to the collection isn't enough, on its own, to cause detailed notifications for all the tickets.

title: Allow setting collection notifications to "everything", "watching" or "nothing".
body:
This provides a way to set the level of involvement that a user has with a collection, and from which we determine the level of notifications to send. Users can be access-only, watching, or being notified about everything.

If you're access-only, you won't get an notifications. If you're watching, you'll only get notifications for the items you're watching (which includes the items you've been assigned, have commented on, etc). If you're set to everything you'll get notifications about all activity in that collection.

This change replaces our previous concept of subscriptions. Where previously you'd subscribe to a collection to get notifications in it, now you'll simply set the notification level on your access.

title: Card "tags" dropdown is no longer subject to the card fragment cache
body:
Previously, if a tag was added to (or removed from) the account, cards' tag dropdowns would not get updated with the changes unless and until the card's fragment cache was invalidated (e.g., a boost). Similar problem to [Missed the save button when turning on "Everyone" access](https://37s.fizzy.37signals.com/buckets/693169850/bubbles/999008259#comment_994777370) fixed in #317.

The fix here is similar to #317:

- Rearrange the _tags and _tag partial, so they are properly nested concerns:
  - `_tags` contains the visible bits on the card, and contains ...
  - `_tag` which is the dialog, and is rendered via a separate turbo frame request so it's not cached with the card
- Wrap both of these partials in a turbo frame
- Cache `_tag` using the bubble and the account
- New controller action: "new" for taggings toggles, which renders the _tag partial
- Updating taggings responds with a turbo stream response that updates the _tags frame

Note that there is new model behavior introduced: the account is touched when tags are added or removed, so we can use the account as a cache key for the tags dialog.

title: Add a sort order to represent "staleness"
body:
Adds a way to sort bubbles by "staleness", and exposes it in the filters.

Staleness is defined here as "the amount of activity score lost". We're effectively considering two things:
- how highly it ranked (in terms of activity) at the time of its last event
- how highly it ranks now

The larger the difference between those two scores, the more "stale" it is.

Once we get a feel for this in practice, there are a couple of things we might want to adjust:
- There's a factor used for the decay curve when calculating the above. It's set to 0.9 which should make the decay close to linear. Lowering that factor should emphasize recent changes more, i.e. items will start to seem stale more quickly. So we can try changing this to see if it helps or hurts.
- We're comparing the score at the time of the items last event, which should mean that if a stale items gets some minor action (like a boost), it doesn't change much. However it's possible we'll want to emphasize an initial burst of activity more, in the face of a trickle of fairly minor activity later. If this seems to be a problem we might want to use something like the highest score the bubble ever had, rather than the more recent (or some blend of the two).

I think we'll just need to try it out for a while to know, though.

title: Move attachments from Account to Bubble
body:
ref: [Need Attachments association on Bubble model](https://37s.fizzy.37signals.com/buckets/693169850/bubbles/999008756)

**Context**

Uploads for comments have previously been associated with the current account, which can make it challenging to figure out what collection/bubble each attachment belongs to. To further complicate things, in the multi-tenant migration, I chose to not deal with unwinding attachments when moving collections into a tenant, and so *all* blobs and attachments were copied to *all* of the new tenants, and as a result there are many orphan attachments.

**This changeset**

The first commit in this PR unwinds the first bit: uploads will be associated with a Bubble, and so the "uploads#create" is now nested under bucket and bubble. "uploads#show" has been moved to a new AttachmentsController and "attachments#show" is bound to the existing "/u/:slug" path. The attachments association is removed from Account and added to Bubble.

The second commit adds a script to unwind the second bit, "which attachment belongs to which bubble?". The script iterates over each attachment in a tenant, and looks for a reference to its slug in any markdown content. If found in comments for exactly one bubble, it sets the attachment's record to be that bubble. After being run, any attachments remaining with a record type of "Account" are almost certainly orphans and can be deleted in the future.

The migration script is safe to run either before or after the application code in the first commit is deployed.

title: Icon helper
body:
This updates the `icon_tag` helper to display icons via CSS masks instead of an image tag. The main benefit here is that we can now color icons arbitrarily just like you would text (instead of `.colorize--black/white`), plus we get dark mode support for free.

A couple notes:

- **Size**: By default, icons are sized at `1em` to match surrounding text. Change the size via the `--icon-size` custom prop. Alternatively, you can also use `font-size` or good old fashioned `block-size` and `inline-size` if you need to.
- **Color**: By default, icon color will match surrounding text. Change the color like you would any text element via `color: <color name>`.

This extends our model to flag cards as being in "doing" or "considering" and adds a couple of buttons to move between both (pending design). It also refactors and tidies up the views for showing collections.

As [per this discussion](https://37s.fizzy.37signals.com/buckets/693169853/bubbles/999008803), we want to keep these states independent of workflows.

This also adds turbo streams to handle changing workflow stages in cards. The reason was a problem with the refreshable frames appearing and disappearing depending on the stage. Since we discussed moving some of these interactions to a frame, I took the chance to do it.

title: Colors on stages
body: Right now colors are arbitrarily applied to cards and it's up to you to come up with your own meaning. As we've seen in our own account, most people aren't coloring them at all and that entire imagined scenario hasn't materialized. This PR changes cards to get inherit their coloring from stages. If they're not in a stage, they're just blue (or whatever the default color ends up being). You can now assign colors to Stages in your Workflows Then when a card is in a particular stage, it inherits that color @jorgemanrubia would you please take a look at this? I've got a basic implementation spiked but I'm sure it could be improved. And there is one big component missing: the card's color should change instantly when you switch stages. There are a number of ways to do that but as the author of the preview/perma setup I thought you might want to decide.

title: Track collection access when viewing cards
body:
@jzimdars @jorgemanrubia this is the idea we discussed the other day for tracking which collections you've accessed recently. It sounded like we're still thinking through that feature idea, so this may not be what we want. But it was quick to try, if you want to play around with it.

The idea here is:
- We keep track of the access time on each user's `Access` to a collection
- Whenever you view a card, we update that collection's access time (at most once every 5 minutes, to avoid a bunch of unnecessary writes).
- We can then order a collection list to show you're "most recently used" collections.

Also note:
- It only updates the access when you view a card from a collection. Just looking at the collection index doesn't do it (currently).
- I've applied the ordering to the collection list on the events#index just so you can see it working. I don't think this is actually where we wanted to show this, though.

title: Add a description field for cards
body: Our previous design leaned on the first comment to add a long text description for cards. This removes that in favor of a description field on `Card` that is displayed on the perma (only). It's a markdown field that can contain formatted text and attachments. Cards now grow taller on the perma to accommodate this extra text resembling documents.

title: Read a card should dismiss all notifications
body:
Previous code assumed that there was a single notification to dismiss for that card, but in practice there can be zero or many. If it's zero, we need to avoid the crash. If it's many, we should dismiss them all.

Also re-rendering the notification stack after dismissing enables us to remove all the removed cards, as well as reveal any older ones that were previously outside the visible page size.

title: Pin without redirect
body:
Use turbo stream response to save on the redirect latency.

It's clear that there's a small saving here, and in this instance the additional code isn't much. But it also reminded me why we often don't do this. If what you need to rerender is a larger chunk, you frequently need to ensure that the action you're triggering has all the information available to render the response. That often lets these concerns bleed together.

But probably worth pushing on a bit more to see where it falls down.

title: Card changes without redirect
body: Let's try to push the rerender rather than redirect envelope a little further and apply it to all changes to the card.

title: Colors
body:
Updated colors for Fizzy!

- Fill out the color palette with 7 values for each color: darkest, darker, dark, medium, light, lighter, and lightest.
- Dark mode color values
- Use CSS variables for workflow colors instead of hex values
- Tweak the golden card styles to be a little more subtle. I also swapped it out for blue in dark mode since dark yellow looks kinda unappealing. Easy enough to change that back if it's a confusing change, though!

A couple notes on usage:

- All `--<color>--dark` values have accessible contrast against `--color-canvas`.
- To use text on a background other than `--color-canvas`, use text with `--<color>-darker/darkest` to keep contrast within the accessible range.
- `--lch-always-black/white` are replaced with `--lch-black/white`. For equivalents that change with dark mode, use `--lch-ink/ink-inverted`.

<mark>**Note**</mark>: I think we'll need to run a db migration for the workflow color change. It works just fine until you try to delete a workflow step:

SQLite3::ConstraintException: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed

title: Plain text mentions
body:
Adds supports for plain text mentions. You can mention other people by entering `@david`, `@dhh` or `@davidh` (same conventions from BC4).

To accomodate mentions, this supports tying notifications to any record, instead of only events. So, the source of a notification can be an event or a mention, as captured by the `source` polymorphic relationship. A mention is not an event, and we should be able to notify them without creating new events. Also, our "notifications" model tracks readings too. We could track readings separately like in BC4, where both mentions and events are `Readable`, but I think this change is simpler and works well.

This doesn't add any UI to assist to add mentions, but lays out the fundation for when we add that.

This is pending some work, opening in case you have feedback on the approach @dhh @kevinmcconnell.

Pending:

- [x] It's duplicating mentions when adding a comment to a message that has a mention in the description.
- [x] Don't re-notify when updating a content with mentions.
- [x] More tests.

As discussed with @dhh, we want to tidy up events a bit https://chat.37signals.com/rooms/440/@41837. I'll work on that after this PR, to keep these smaller.

body:
This generalizes our system of events. Before, events were tied to cards. Now events will be tied to *eventables*, with "cards" and "comments" being a kind of eventable.

Instead of registering comment's creations at the card level, they will carry their own event now. This will naturally solve the problem where deleting a comment leaves the event comment-less (see [this](https://37s.fizzy.37signals.com/collections/693169850/cards/999008952)). 

This discharges the event from knowing so much about the system, and, also, opens the events system to be used with other models, such as collections or accounts, if we needed to.

Events will now be contained in collections, which we'll use to query accessible events more efficiently.

This also reworks the system to render the home timeline, introducing a new `User::DayTimeline` model, reusing the our `Filter` object and, in general, tightening up the related a code quite a bit.

Scoping timelines to whole days comes from our pagination system and how it plays with the layout design. This could be problematic for huge accounts with tons of events on a given day, so we may need to revisit in the future. I kept that out of the scope with this change.

Another change is that, we will now prefix event's actions with the name of the target model. E.g: "card_published" or "comment_created".

- [x] Script to migrate existing events (action name is prefixed now).
- [x] Create local time format for matching current behavior for titles in the timeline.
- [x] Test well in staging: compare timelines, test pagination, etc.
- [x] Fix: collection cookie persistence is not working.
- [x] Tests.

title: Introduce a recursive descent parser for the Fizzy Do command line
body:
Using a hand-written recursive descent parser instead of a LALR parser generator (like lex/yacc or rex/racc) because IMHO it's easier to understand, extend, and debug. It also allows us to be a bit more error-tolerant where we need to.

The AST I'm introducing here is pretty simple, and I'm not tracking token location because my assumption is that the parsed strings are all going to be short.

I'll also note that this approach, and some of the API patterns, borrow from the Ruby "syntax tree" projects, see https://github.com/ruby-syntax-tree for other living examples.

ref: https://3.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/37331921/documents/8608517933

---

I'm pushing this PR to get feedback on this approach; if nobody is opposed, then next steps would probably be:

- implement the remaining pieces of the syntax/grammar
- make the parse error reporting clearer (e.g., when the CLI command is incomplete or there are additional tokens that can't be parsed)

title: Fizzy Do (initial)
body:
Very initial version of Fizzy Do. It features:

- Go to card by number.
- Visit `@someone's` profile.
- Assign cards. The target cards will be derived from the screen you are located at (card perma or index).
- Show history of recent commands.
- Undo assignments.

The input field is a plain text editor. We'll use a richer approach with inline suggestions after we make a call on the editor.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c83c2068-4a7a-4c62-8e37-d6a64e302b94

Regarding the model, a user will now have a list of commands. Different types of command classes inherit from a base one using STI. A command encapsulates how it's executed and undone.

Pending:

- [x] Test

title: Fizz Do with AI
body:
Adds LLM processing to the *Fizzy Do* bar, enabling:

- Filtering cards using natural language. E.g: `cards assigned to jz`.
- Act on cards using natural language: E.g: `close cards assigned to jz`.
- Get insight on cards: E.g: `summarize this card`.

This is all quite experimental. The system to translate natural language to commands seems powerful enough to stay. We need to experiment with the insight system and explore other use cases in future PRs.

## LLM used

This utilizes OpenAI's API, specifically GPT-4.1 nano (the most affordable chat model), and the Ruby gem [`ruby_llm`](https://github.com/crmne/ruby_llm). For embeds it's using `text-embedding-3-small`.

The gem ruby_llm has a minimal API surface and allows you to switch between different models easily, making it handy for this early stage. We can explore other options down the road.

## Design

### Translating to commands

For querying cards and acting on them the system uses an LLM to translate natural language into commands. The output of the LLM will have this form:

```
{
  context: {
  ...
  }

  commands: [ "/command1 param", "/command2" ]
}
```

- `commands:` uses the commands Fizzy supports to act on cards. The user may well enter those directly too.
- `context`: contains properties compatible with our filtering system.

Both are optional: the LLM may decide that the current context is ok, and no new context is needed to act on it. Or it might decide that the whole operation is about filtering cards, so no commands are required.

The final result is a `Command::Composite` composite command that aggregates N child commands. 

### Getting insight

To get insight, there is a new `/insight command` that uses a different prompt combined with a context. The context (cards and comments) could be extracted from the current page or be a new one if the LLM determines so.

E.g:

- `summarize` when you are viewing a card will summarize the current card.
- `summarize cards assigned to JZ` will create a new context, redirect you there, and then summarize those cards.

When translating natural languages to commands, the LLM may determine to include an `/insight` command using the system explained above.

## Embedded vector searches

Also experimentally, this PR adds vector embeds using [this extension](https://github.com/asg017/sqlite-vec) to perform semantic searches.

## Pending

- [ ] Make links work in prompts.
- [x] Tests.
- [x] Create production credentials for the API.
- [x] Address feedback by Donal.
- [ ] Design review by JZ.

title: Activity dom
body:
The original idea here was to make the activity feed look nicer on mobile. In looking at the code, though, all the events were being placed in a single DOM element and arranged into columns via CSS grid. This made it tricky to lay things out on smaller viewports, and I suspect this approach wouldn't be ideal for screen readers. I reworked the DOM a bit so that events are grouped by type (added, updated, and closed) and placed into their own dedicated columns. We're still using CSS grid to space out events properly like before; the main difference is that we only do this on larger viewports now. Mobile view is an easy-to browse single-column stacked list. #### So instead of this… ```html

Updated

Closed

…
``` #### We're doing this this… ```html

title: Generate "closing soon" bubbles in javascript
body:
In https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/pull/406, the "closing soon" bubbles were added. However, as described in [Auto-close bubbles aren't adding up](https://37s.fizzy.37signals.com/collections/693169850/cards/999009091), these bubbles are part of the cached card and so as time passes, the "closes in N days" doesn't change unless the card is touched.

This PR moves all of the bubble markup into a formatter used by the "local time" stimulus controller, and the formatter will only be triggered if the time is within `within` days from now.

I don't feel great about having the markup in a javascript string, so if someone can recommend a better pattern for this, please let me know.

The addition of the `within` attribute (to only display the bubble within the reminder period) is a pretty clear smell. **Should we just put this into a separate controller**, rather than extending the "local time" controller further than it was originally intended?

title: Considering bubble
body:
This adds a bubble to the Doing column when cards are about to move back to the Considering column.

I think "Reconsider in" would be a nice label for the bubble, but it simply doesn't fit unless we make the text really small or cram the characters too close together. Right now I'm just using "Consider in" because it fits better. Open to suggestions!

**Note**: This will eventually need to end up being inserted via JS so we don't bork caching.

- Update engageable.rb to include methods for timing out when to show the reconsider bubble
- Update bubble partial to accept different label text
- Extract bubble css into its own file
- Bubbles now take on the card color instead of always being blue
- Create dedicated space on either side of the card columns so the bubble is visible on smaller viewports

![CleanShot 2025-05-14 at 15 44 10@2x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21d04e0d-f344-43c8-8aad-a1d5b8e3ded0)

title: Introduce a stimulus controller for bubbles
body:
The "closing soon" bubbles were introduced in #406, and the "falling back" bubbles in #500. However, these bubbles are part of the cached card and so as time passes, the relative time doesn't change unless the card is touched.

This PR introduces a stimulus controller for bubbles, which takes care of:

- making the bubble visible during the reminder period
- calculating the relative number of days until entropy kicks in
- rendering appropriate text around the day count

ref: https://37s.fizzy.37signals.com/collections/693169850/cards/999009091

cc @andyra

Changelog

5.24.0

Features

  • Add new sidekiq config report_only_dead_jobs (#2581)

  • Add max_nesting of 10 to breadcrumbs data serialization (#2583)

  • Add sidekiq config propagate_traces to control trace header injection (#2588)

    If you use schedulers you can get one large trace with all your jobs which is undesirable. We recommend using the following to propagate traces only from the Rails server and not elsewhere.

    config.sidekiq.propagate_traces = false unless Rails.const_defined?('Server')

  • Only expose active_storage keys on span data if send_default_pii is on (#2589)

  • Add new Sentry.logger for Structured Logging feature (#2620).

    To enable structured logging you need to turn on the enable_logs configuration option:

    Sentry.init do |config|
  # ... your setup ...
  config.enable_logs = true
end

    Once you configured structured logging, you get access to a new Sentry.logger object that can be used as a regular logger with additional structured data support:

    Sentry.logger.info("User logged in", user_id: 123)

    Sentry.logger.error("Failed to process payment",
transaction_id: "tx_123",
error_code: "PAYMENT_FAILED"
)

    You can also use message templates with positional or hash parameters:

    Sentry.logger.info("User %{name} logged in", name: "Jane Doe")

    Sentry.logger.info("User %s logged in", ["Jane Doe"])

    Any other arbitrary attributes will be sent as part of the log event payload:

    # Here `user_id` and `action` will be sent as extra attributes that Sentry Logs UI displays
Sentry.logger.info("User %{user} logged in", user: "Jane", user_id: 123, action: "create")

... (truncated)

body:
Extract a Card::Entropy concern to encompass behavior related to auto-closing and auto-reconsidering.

Note that putting this code in a single place reveals an asymmetry between the actions:

- Auto-closing period is an optional attribute of a collection
- Auto-reconsidering period is hard-coded to 30 days for all collections

and suggests some opportunities to make the language we use more consistent.

body:
Things looked off because an extra grid column was getting introduced on the right. Seems like the browser didn't know what column to put the column headers in some cases (not sure why some and not all cases, though), so it created another column to drop it in.

We currently place grid positions on all the cards, but not on the headers. To fix this, we just need to be explicit about what column the headers go in.

title: Tray shadows
body:
To get a shadow behind the tray content, we need to use relative position for the tray__items (instead of absolute). So this involved quite a bit of refactoring! The upside is that we do less work to position elements and hand that off to the browser.

title: Handle single items better
body:
Handles single items in trays better.

- If there's a single Pin, clicking will just go to the card instead of the usual action of expanding the tray dialog.
- If there's a single notification, we still open the dialog to reveal the notification actions

title: Add height/width values for images and videos
body:
Adding dimensions to images will properly set the aspect ratio, which means no layout shift as images load. Cool! 👍 I'm having trouble with videos, though. Ideally, we'd add an aspect-ratio style attribute to the video tag, like so: ```erb <%= tag.video src: rails_blob_path(blob), style: "aspect-ratio: #{width} / #{height};", … %> ``` When I do this, however, the `style` tag gets stripped. In fact, most attributes other than `class` don't end up in the DOM. If I add this element to the ERB file, for instance, only the `class` attribute shows up: ```html
``` Maybe this is being sanitized at some point before it reaches the browser?

title: Remove tray padding around comments
body:
This removes the extra padding around comments that was being applied on larger viewports. Looks like the original idea was to keep the comment content tucked safely between the tray cards, which makes sense! But this effectively makes the comment section pretty narrow from about 1280–1580px, and it actually gets wider on viewports under 1280px.

Instead, we can just set a max width on comments and not account for the tray cards. There will be a bit of content overlap here, but it's not much and you just need to scroll down an extra 24-ish px at most. Seems like a profitable trade-off.

title: Entropy improvements
body:
This adds a new setting for parameterizing the reconsideration interval, and introduces default account-level settings for entropy parameters.

Before, we had a single parameter defined at the collection level. I extracted a new entity `Entropy::Configuration` that aggregates both intervals. A collection will now have an "entropy configuration", or it will default to the account's when not set.

We decided that entropy handling is mandatory, you can't opt out. I tried to reflect this in the code. E.g: before we had a check to see if a collection was `auto_closing?`, which didn't make sense anymore.

To edit the account-level entropy configuraiton, this introduces a new "account settings" screen. Pending to review all this with @jzimdars.

cc @kevinmcconnell @flavorjones 

- [ ] Backfill account "entropy configurations" in production

title: Knobs
body:
This stubs out the knob UI for the collection settings page. It's not hooked up to anything at the moment.

It's basically just a styled radio field with the knob pointing to the selected option; as such, it's fully keyboard accessible. The range input is there to provide mouse interactions with the knob UI. Drag it left/right, and a bit of JS will set the correct radio option. The range input is hidden from screen readers and doesn't actually store any data.

I've set it up so that we can feed in an arbitrary number of options and the knob UI will adjust itself to fit everything (up to a point, of course! 20+ options will look bad).

title: Bump rack from 3.1.15 to 3.1.16
body:
Bumps [rack](https://github.com/rack/rack) from 3.1.15 to 3.1.16.
Changelog

Sourced from rack's changelog.

Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. For info on how to format all future additions to this file please reference Keep A Changelog.

Unreleased

SPEC Changes

  • Request environment keys must now be strings. #2310, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Add nil as a valid return from a Response body.to_path (#2318, [@​MSP-Greg])

Added

  • Introduce Rack::VERSION constant. (#2199, [@​ioquatix])
  • ISO-2022-JP encoded parts within MIME Multipart sections of an HTTP request body will now be converted to UTF-8. (#2245, @​nappa)

Changed

  • Invalid cookie keys will now raise an error. (#2193, [@​ioquatix])
  • Rack::MediaType#params now handles empty strings. (#2229, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Avoid unnecessary calls to the ip_filter lambda to evaluate Request#ip (#2287, [@​willbryant])
  • Only calculate Request#ip once per request (#2292, [@​willbryant])

Deprecated

  • Rack::Auth::AbstractRequest#request is deprecated without replacement. (#2229, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Rack::Request#parse_multipart (private method designed to be overridden in subclasses) is deprecated without replacement. (#2229, [@​jeremyevans])

Removed

  • Rack::Request#values_at is removed. (#2200, [@​ioquatix])
  • Rack::Logger is removed with no replacement. (#2196, [@​ioquatix])
  • Automatic cache invalidation in Rack::Request#{GET,POST} has been removed. (#2230, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Support for CGI::Cookie has been removed. (#2332, [@​ioquatix])

Fixed

  • Rack::RewindableInput::Middleware no longer wraps a nil input. (#2259, @​tt)
  • Fix NoMethodError in Rack::Request#wrap_ipv6 when x-forwarded-host is empty. (#2270, @​oieioi)
  • Fix the specification for SERVER_PORT which was incorrectly documented as required to be an Integer if present - it must be a String containing digits only. (#2296, [@​ioquatix])
  • SERVER_NAME and HTTP_HOST are now more strictly validated according to the relevant specifications. (#2298, [@​ioquatix])

title: Public collections
body:
Support making collections public.

This adds a setting to publish collections and getting a shareable and non-discoverable URL for them like `http://37signals.fizzy.localhost:3006/public/collections/VPPdWo81PN7uirmwtzNU1gXd`.

Public collections are read-only. You can only see the cards.

title: Responsive trays
body:
This gets the trays working on small viewports. There are a couple things we may want to tweak here, but this is a functional improvement over what we have now. Here's how it works:

### Instead of a stack of cards, we'll show an icon for each tray

If there are 1+ items in a tray, we'll show a red dot. I could imagine wanting something a little different here (like a count), but this gets the idea across for the time being.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c84e4316-147b-434b-a4e0-d494a13be344)

### When you tap the icon, the tray takes up the whole footer

One potential issue is closing the expanded notifications tray. Right now, you have to tap outside the dialog to close it, but we may want to add a dedicated close button if that doesn't feel right. I didn't include that here because I couldn't see a straight shot.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6afe839-3fb0-4705-a3a3-04503c97cfba)

### Blank slate

When there aren't items, the Pin tray is simply disabled. The notifications tray is still enabled to allow access to the links to notification settings and index pages.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9eadbeaa-4789-437a-8dd6-8457a64fae75)

title: Mobile columns
body:
Mobile improvements for the Collections page. Basically, just stacking the columns and making the headers/filters sticky.

At first, I tried making the columns horizontally scrollable, so you'd see the Considering columns by default, then swipe right to see the Doing column. That didn't work well, however, since that kind of interaction works best when you have content that peeks from the edge of the screen. I couldn't find a way to do that was unambiguous and not-weird-looking, so this stacked approach gets the job done a different way.

I ended up adding padding on both sides of the cards to allow room for the bubbles and keep things looking balanced. I'm not 100% sold on this approach, but it did look rather uncomfortable to have a gap just on the right or left.

title: Drag and drop cards to move between doing/considering
body:
This adds support to D&D cards between doing and considering.

For the implementation, I went with a "drag and drop" stimulus controller, instead of doing with a more complex "sortable controller" (such as the one we had in KIA, which was heavily inspired by the one in Writebook). When/if we add sorting for cards, we'll complicate things. For now, we wanted a way to drop cards between columns, so I focused on that.

Since the sorting is implicit, when dropping a card, we re-render the whole column in a turbo stream response. This won't feel as smooth as handling the placement in the client, but it saves us from having to recreate the different sorting options in the client. I think it feels good enough.

As per the controller, I went with a dedicated "cards / drops controller" instead of reusing the "engagements" one, since the handling of the response is quite different and specific to the interaction. I think a single endpoint that handles the change based on the target column makes sense here (versus different actions on a more UI-agnostic resource).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0262f17f-1573-46ff-b525-731997cbe6c4

Pending:

- [x] Design/styles.
- [x] Tidy up code a bit.
- [x] Only make draggable card previews in "Doing" and "Considering".
- [x] Tests.

title: Launchpad integration: step 1
body:
- Account belongs to Signal::Account
- User belongs to Signal::User
- Add request details to Current
- Launchpad login works for existing 37id identities
- Introduce a Signup model and integrate with QB/37id
- Introduce a Signups controller and support new and existing identities
- Put the Signups controllers behind HTTP basic auth for now (internal only, see 1password)
- Seeds and fixtures updated to load properly
- Beta environment QB account names will include "(Beta)" to differentiate on Launchpad
- Implement the QB "plans" API
- Script to bootstrap existing accounts and users into SignalID accounts and users

At the end of this, after running the bootstrap script, people will be able to login via _either_ Launchpad or the existing sessions controller. This is not permanent, but something to hopefully ease the transition and accommodate users that do not have a SignalId::Identity.

Note that signups will work, but the created tenant will be unusable because the subdomain will not have a TLS cert. This is not permanent, and will be fixed once we finishg the move to account-slug tenanting.

cc @jorgemanrubia @kevinmcconnell

@jzimdars, I was working on the nav changes we talked about (getting the Settings/Notifications buttons on the same level as the title on the Collection page), and came up with something that touched https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/pull/657 as well. Lemme run this by you:

- On the Collection page, I don't love the Home button on the some line as the collection title. It's is more of a global nav thing, so it feels better to have it at the top along with the Fizzy menu.

title: Focus hover styles
body:
This updates how we're doing focus and hover states for interactive elements. A quick rundown:

- All interactive elements have the same blue ring when focusing by keyboard. You won't see these with mouse interactions. We can tweak this to suit using globally the `--focus-ring-size/color/offset` variables.
- Text inputs no longer have a hover effect.
- Buttons now have a filter applied when hovering which darkens them a bit (or lightens them when in dark mode) instead of a gray ring.
- Tweaked the `[aria-selected]` styles for popovers and prompt menus.
- Removed all the references to `--hover-size/color`
- Added hover effects in a few places where they were missing: column filters, Fizzy menu, workflow previews, and the like.

title: Notification links
body:
A couple changes to trays:

- Notification actions are now at the top of the expanded tray (instead of a separate "actions" section below).
- Added a "remove pin" button to pinned items. It's quite nice to quickly remove a pinned item without visiting the page first.
- It's now easier to close the notifications tray on mobile since there's a dedicated toggle button. Works just like the Pinned tray now.

The main thing I'm not sure about is if it's clear when there are more unread notifications than will fit in the list or not. I had a red dot next to "See more…" at first—which worked well—but it was also just a lot of red dots. Let me know what you think, @jzimdars!

title: Fizzy do improvements
body:
- Reworked prompt, more concise, less ambiguous, better.
- Update LLM model to "mini" from "nano". It works noticeably better.
- Add support for filtering by stage.
- Inject collection names and stage names in the prompt for better interpretation.

Includes also fix for https://fizzy.37signals.com/5986089/collections/2/cards/1128

To test if this is good enough before abandoning for v1.

title: Resolve stages
body:
- Consider all the stages through accessible collections. The previous approach was only considering the card screens.
- Resolve stage names emitted by the AI translator properly.

title: Script to load a production db in development
body:
to make testing Fizzy Do easier.

Also: Signup class properly uses the queenbee_id instead of the subdomain for the tenant name, which should have been in #665.

cc @jorgemanrubia

title: Make sure it doesn't infer custom abbreviations when matching user names
body: E.g: it was inferring "jzimdars" for "jz", which we'll fail to resolve

title: Add /user command
body:
The LLM was relying on it. Having it missing resulted in a stack overflow error!

https://fizzy.37signals.com/5986089/collections/7/cards/1135

title: Make sure the image variants we use are preprocessed
body:
... to avoid implicitly creating a variant during a GET to a read replica, which will raise an exception and cause the image to fail to load.

This feels pretty brittle, to be honest, and we'll need to be careful in the future about creating and using new variants; we will probably need to backfill the new variant for existing images because we can't guarantee that they will be created implicitly/lazily if the GET lands on the replica.

ref: https://fizzy.37signals.com/5986089/collections/7/cards/942

I tried using container queries with `container-type: size` on the card, but it completely borked the card layout. Here, I'm just removing the aspect-ratio, which prevents the stamp from getting huge when the text wraps. |Before|After| |--|--| |||

body: Adds web push notifications in browsers and PWAs on mobile and desktop (where supported). The implementation is largely based on the one from ONCE/Campfire which was nicely abstracted and field-tested. The UI flows were adapted for Fizzy and updated to match current web push support. The UI to subscribe is on the Notifications Settings screen. The screen also detects the status of push subscriptions and support and advises the user on how to clear common roadblocks (usually some layer of Notification settings). title: AI summaries
body:
This adds AI summaries in the timeline. [Read description](https://3.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/37331921/todos/8882769136#__recording_8882795191).

## Internal design

AI summaries are expensive to generate; they literally cost money 😅. For the design, I considered:

* We want to cache them as much as possible. E.g: if two users in two different time zones with different collection accesses are seeing the same set of events for a given day in the timeline, they should see the same summary.
* Summaries are filter-sensitive. Changing filters will result in different summaries.
* Losing access to collections should invalidate summaries if they referred to contents you no longer have access to.

The solution I went with is using a record "activity summary" that is unique on a key that we calculate as a hash of the event ids. When rendering the activity for a set of cards, if there is a summary in place for them, we show it. If not, we calculate it in a background job and we show it with a broadcasted turbo stream.

This way, if the set of cards change, summaries will get generated automatically under demand. E.g: when changing filters or losing access to collections. Also, this guarantees that we make the minimal number of AI requests.

I considered using regular Rails caching, but it seemed too weak. The summaries we generate are meaningful pieces of information. I think it makes sense to make them a first-class citizen. 

I also considered using a more fine-grained design, where the "summary record" links with the events via a join table. This felt too heavy, especially considering we could have tons of events involved in a given summary.

Finally, I also discarded a "user-level" caching system, because I think it's important we reuse across users as much as possible. I think it will be quite realistic that most users in a given company will see exactly the same summaries, because they all see the same activity.

As a tradeoff, it's not easy to *clean* these summaries in a fine-grained way. E.g: if you select a certain filter for a certain date, that will generate a summary and we'll persist forever. I think we could do fine with some rough cleanup approach with a cron job: e.g: eliminate summaries older than 3 months. Since they are generated on the fly, this should be a pretty simple approach.

Also, down the road we could explore generating these summaries proactively (e.g: in the beginning of every day, so that the first user that request them doesn't have to wait a few seconds for them).

## Pending:

- [x] Tests
- [x] Design

title: Removed redundant div
body:
Fixes an issue where the cursor in Firefox was disappearing when adding a description on a new card. The culprit was some CSS that hides the empty DOM elements that Lexical creates when no description is added (`


`). It takes up space, so we want to hide it if there's nothing to show. We only want to do that when viewing the card, though, not editing, so I made that CSS more targeted. It's not clear why this was an issue in Firefox and no other browser, but in any case, it's fixed now!

title: Hide placeholder when list is inserted
body: The `lexical-editor--empty` class controls the visibility of the placeholder. Right now, the placeholder is visible when there aren't characters. Since an empty list is just a DOM element without characters, the placeholder is still visible. Here, I'm amending the CSS to show the placeholder only if lists aren't present.
