title: Bump rouge from 4.5.2 to 4.6.0
body:
Bumps [rouge](https://github.com/rouge-ruby/rouge) from 4.5.2 to 4.6.0.
Release notes

Sourced from rouge's releases.

v4.6.0

This release introduces support for the Bicep language and enhances several existing lexers. We've added Ada 2022 features including the parallel keyword and improved syntax for arrays. The Python lexer now supports the match and case keywords and has been updated with Python 3 builtin keywords, functions, and exceptions. C# lexer improvements include Unicode character support and a refactoring of keywords to class methods. The TOML lexer now properly handles inline tables in arrays. We've also enhanced file detection with Docker file name patterns, Terraform *.tfvars files, and improved disambiguation between Objective-C and Mathematica lexers. Additionally, Ruby 3.4 has been added to our CI build process. Thanks to all our contributors for their valuable work on making Rouge better!

Full Changelog: https://github.com/rouge-ruby/rouge/compare/v4.5.2...v4.6.0

title: Trays keyboard nav
body: Add hotkeys and keyboard (arrow up/down) navigation to Pins and Notifications trays: Also: - Allows navigating Notifications index by keyboard. - Changes pinned cards to use pin icon for unpin action instead of x. - Reverses the pin icon asset so it points at the card instead of away. - Makes `.tray__hat` inert when the dialog is closed. Because the invisible tray toggle isn't as tall as the cards, it was possible to inadvertently click through to the hat and end up on Notification Settings (or Index or Mark all as Read). - Adds an option to reverse navigate to the navigable-lists controller so you the arrow goes in the expected direction in the trays.

title: Lightbox improvements
body:
- Add a transition to the lightbox dialog. It involves a bit of JS since we need to wait for the CSS transition to finish before resetting the image src.

title: Fizzy Ask
body:
[Fizzy Ask](https://3.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/37331921/messages/8885137052) is an interactive way to  explore your Fizzy cards and comments through a conversation.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7ac3cf9-b0a5-4cb2-b62c-b2f001e08bd2

## How the chat works

The LLM can access your Fizzy cards, collections, comments and users through tools and RubyLLM's tool calling interface.
A tool is similar to a controller. Its responsibility is to gather data and produce a response.

Most of the chat logic was ported over from campfire.

The chat modal is a special response from the command parser. This was inspired by the insight response.
I made it generic so that it can show any turbo frame.

## Pointers for reviewers

A good starting place to review this is the case statement in the Command::Parser and the Command::Ask class.
They handle the creation of a conversation for a user and posting the initial message when they type /ask

I'd recommend then going to the CommandsController, and then to the Conversation and Conversation::Message classes.

I'm not particularly happy with how the tools turned out because I had to include the view-layer / serialization in them.
All suggestions for how to improve them are welcome.
The current interface feels a bit clunky. I'd like to replace it with something like:
```ruby
page = extract_page(cards, page: params[:page])
render "cards/index", page: page
```
But that requires me to add a lot of HTTP API-specific code which would make this PR unwieldy - it would have both Fizzy Ask and 30% of the API work in it.
So I opted to go with a clunky interface for now and return to improve it once the API is in place.

Also, as this is an experimental feature, I kept the filters as separate namespaced objects specific to each tool.
They currently do filtering and sanitization, but I'd like to move them to the model if they will be used in the API and have them do just filtering.
I had this kind of interface in mind:
```ruby
cards.filtered_by(**filters)
# or, maybe
# cards.search(**filters)
# cards.search("foobar", **filters)
```

title: Tooltips
body:
Adds tooltips to the icon buttons. Since we already have screen reader labels, we can just expose those visually on hover. To get this working, just add a `tooltip` class to anything with a `<span class="for-screen-reader">` child.

I should point out that this isn't particularly sophisticated. Tooltips aren't aware of the screen boundary, for instance (so it sometimes get clipped). There's also not any mechanism to position it anywhere other than above the button. These limitations may make this a bit funky in certain circumstances, so let's try it out and see how it feels.

title: Hack for Safari sticky-footer-while-transitioning bug
body:
Safari won't position sticky elements correctly until after its ancestor's animations/transitions have completed. The visual result for us is that the sticky footer in the Fizzy menu jumps when you open it, which looks crazy!

This hack positions the footer absolutely (which Safari renders correctly during the transition) until the popover transition is complete, then applies sticky positioning.

Here's a before/after (transitions slowed down and BG colors added to highlight the effect, but they aren't in the PR):

title: Popup orientation
body: This adds a JS helper to assist with orienting elements so they don't hang off the edge of the screen. Useful for popovers, tooltips, etc. To use it, import the module into a controller, then call `orient(element)` on the thing you want to keep within the viewport. The module will add a CSS class (`orient-left|right|top`), which you can use to position the element. This PR adds orientation awareness to the dialog element, so all popovers should now stay within the bounds of the screen. I'll take on tooltips next! |Before|After| |--|--| |||

title: Bundled notification emails
body: Adds support for sending emails that aggregate unread notifications periodically. This adds a new option to receive periodic emails that bundle notifications: Emails will look like this: ## Approach This introduces a new model `Notification::Bundle` that represents a window of time containing unread notifications. We don't link the notifications directly, but we query the unread notifications in the window of time when we need to. I went with this design because the nature of notifications enable it (immutable, frozen in time), and it's lighter and simpler than creating explicit links from notification to bundle. So the idea is that, when bundling is enabled, it will bundle new notifications. That means that we'll verify that either there is a pending bundle with a window that includes the new notification, or we create one. There is a cron process that, periodically, deliver emails for all the bundles that are due. For the settings, it introduces a new model `User::Settings` to store the bundle notification frequency. I added a model instead of adding a new column to `User` as we're likely adding more user settings in the future, to avoid ending up with a bloated user model. ## Pending: - [x] Test in beta - [x] Add unsubscribe link - [x] Review settings screen design ## Deploy Script to create default settings for users after deploying: ```ruby ApplicationRecord.with_each_tenant do |tenant| User.find_each do |user| user.create_settings! end end ```

title: Make Fizzy Ask respond with an error message when a response fails to generate
body: Sometimes the response job will fail for expected or unexpected reasons. We should communicate to the user that an error happened instead of leaving the user's conversation stuck in the thinking state with no feedback. This PR adds some error handling to the response generator job which, in case an error occurs, responds to the user to let them know that their question wasn't processed and that they should try again. This also unlocks the conversation so that they can ask another question if they'd like. The error messages differ slightly. For rate-limit and service availability error I've made Fizzy respond with a message saying that it's too busy at the moment. And for all other errors I made it respond with the Rails classic "Something went wrong". Both errors instruct the user to try again.

title: Update Beamer configuration to switchable version
body:
- Updates Fizzy to use the new "switchable" version of Beamer
- Simplifies the deployment configuration: instead of two separate `web` and `web-replica` roles, we now just have the usual `web`. Aside from job configuration (which we're working on separately), the deployment of each app node is now identical.
- Beamer node configuration is now automatic. The first time the `fizzy-beamer` accessory boots, it'll init the cluster, using the hostname provided in `$KAMAL_HOST` to name it.
- There's a new Kamal alias that can be used to set or change the direction of replication:

      PRIMARY=fizzy-app-101 bin/kamal switch -d production

Note that there are two caveats to using `kamal switch` right now:
  - Until we set up a moveable job worker, replication is only valid from fizzy-app-101 -> fizzy-app-102. If you run `kamal switch` to move the primary to -102, there's nothing there to run jobs.
  - Switching doesn't currently update the load balancer either. This is because we have some funky inconsistent naming in the LB to get around the fact that it's piggybacked onto one of the app servers. We should move it to another node, and then the hosts/ports will be consistent and we can an add alias to move that too.)

/cc @flavorjones

title: Correct file attachment layout and simplify icons
body:
After touching up the attachment styles for Lexxy, I noticed a couple broken spots and optimizations we could be making in Fizzy as well:

- Move the preview styles under the `.attachment--preview` class instead of relying on `.attachment:is(figure)` since all attachments use the figure tag
- Prune the base attachment class and move more specific styles to the respective modifier classes (e.g. `--file|preview`)
- Instead of overwriting styles for each icon color, we can simply pass in a color variable and consume that in the base icon class. A nice way to remove a bunch of lines!

title: Tweak the header actions width
body: The header actions width was a touch too small, which made the Add a Card button on the home screen bunched up on Firefox. A reminder why magic numbers are smelly, although in this case perhaps the best option.

title: Disable access switch for current user
body:
Current users shouldn't be able to remove themselves from a collection. It just feels weird to have the ability to lock yourself out of a collection. This also addresses the edge case where you could uncheck _everybody_ from a collection, which would require a support call to let anyone have access again.

- https://fizzy.37signals.com/5986089/collections/2/cards/738

title: Bump sentry-rails from 5.26.0 to 5.27.0
body:
Bumps [sentry-rails](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-ruby) from 5.26.0 to 5.27.0.
Changelog

Sourced from sentry-rails's changelog.

5.27.0

Feature

  • Propagated sampling rates as specified in Traces docs (#2671)

  • Support for Rails ActiveSupport log subscribers (#2690)

  • Support for defining custom Rails log subscribers that work with Sentry Structured Logging (#2689)

    Rails applications can now define custom log subscribers that integrate with Sentry's structured logging system. The feature includes built-in subscribers for ActionController, ActiveRecord, ActiveJob, and ActionMailer events, with automatic parameter filtering that respects Rails' config.filter_parameters configuration.

    To enable structured logging with Rails log subscribers:

    Sentry.init do |config|
  # ... your setup ...

    Make sure structured logging is enabled
    

    config.enable_logs = true
    

    Enable default Rails log subscribers (ActionController and ActiveRecord)
    

    config.rails.structured_logging.enabled = true
    
end

    To configure all subscribers:

    Sentry.init do |config|
  # ... your setup ...

    Make sure structured logging is enabled
    

    config.enable_logs = true
    

    Enable Rails log subscribers
    

    config.rails.structured_logging.enabled = true
    

    Add ActionMailer and ActiveJob subscribers
    

    config.rails.structured_logging.subscribers.update(
    
action_mailer: Sentry::Rails::LogSubscribers::ActionMailerSubscriber,
    
active_job: Sentry::Rails::LogSubscribers::ActiveJobSubscriber
    
)
    
end

    You can also define custom log subscribers by extending the base class:

    class MyCustomSubscriber < Sentry::Rails::LogSubscriber
  attach_to :my_component

Changelog

Sourced from sentry-ruby's changelog.

5.27.0

Feature

  • Propagated sampling rates as specified in Traces docs (#2671)

  • Support for Rails ActiveSupport log subscribers (#2690)

  • Support for defining custom Rails log subscribers that work with Sentry Structured Logging (#2689)

    Rails applications can now define custom log subscribers that integrate with Sentry's structured logging system. The feature includes built-in subscribers for ActionController, ActiveRecord, ActiveJob, and ActionMailer events, with automatic parameter filtering that respects Rails' config.filter_parameters configuration.

    To enable structured logging with Rails log subscribers:

    Sentry.init do |config|
  # ... your setup ...

    Make sure structured logging is enabled
    

    config.enable_logs = true
    

    Enable default Rails log subscribers (ActionController and ActiveRecord)
    

    config.rails.structured_logging.enabled = true
    
end

    To configure all subscribers:

    Sentry.init do |config|
  # ... your setup ...

    Make sure structured logging is enabled
    

    config.enable_logs = true
    

    Enable Rails log subscribers
    

    config.rails.structured_logging.enabled = true
    

    Add ActionMailer and ActiveJob subscribers
    

    config.rails.structured_logging.subscribers.update(
    
action_mailer: Sentry::Rails::LogSubscribers::ActionMailerSubscriber,
    
active_job: Sentry::Rails::LogSubscribers::ActiveJobSubscriber
    
)
    
end

    You can also define custom log subscribers by extending the base class:

    class MyCustomSubscriber < Sentry::Rails::LogSubscriber
  attach_to :my_component

... (truncated)

title: 404s on notifications
body:
This solves several problems related to getting a 404 when following notifications:

1. Deleting a notification source would leave a broken notification until the user reloaded the app.
2. Moving a notification to an accessible collection would leave the notification broken until the user reloaded the app.
3. Moving a notification to an inaccessible collection would leave the notification permanently broken.

The implemented solutions:

1. Broadcast a stream to remove the notification.
2. Flatten the notification resources so that we don't include the collection in the path.
3. Run a job that will remove the notifications for those users who lost access with the change.

See:

- https://fizzy.37signals.com/5986089/collections/2/cards/1588

title: Webhooks
body:
## How it works

Webhooks hook into (pun intended) the events model.

For every event that's created a WebhookDispatch job is spawned that checks which webhooks should get triggered and then triggers them.

I've used the new Continuable API here to avoid double deliveries in case a job gets stopped midway through the iteration.

Triggering a Webhook creates a new pending Delivery.
Each Delivery has an after create callback that enqueues a job that then performs the delivery.
I used the limits concurrency method here to preserve causality as much as possible.
It's not a guarantee that the hooks will get delivered in order, but it help preserve the order in most cases.

The delivery performs a POST request and stores the request headers, response status code, response headers and response error on the delivery object. It also tracks the state of the delivery - is it pending, in progress, completed or errored.

There are four security mechanisms in place:

First, all deliveries are signed with a secret that's only visible in the UI. This allows the recipient to verify that the hook is really from us. I used standard HMAC SHA256 for this - it's fast, simple and reliable.

Second, all deliveries have a timestamp in the header to prevent replay attacks.

Third, at delivery, all URLs are resolved and checked if they target loopback, link-local and other similar private networks that are often targeted for internal DDoS attacks.

Fourth, all webhooks are periodically checked for delinquent behavior. If all deliveries to a webhook fail in 12h, and there were more than 50 deliveres, the webhook is considered to be delinquent and gets deactivated. Users can re-activate a webhook on their own.

For serialization, regular Rails views are used.

## UI development
For testing the UI, run this to get two webhooks with everything attached:
```ruby
tenant = "735464785" # change this to your tenant
ApplicationRecord.with_tenant(tenant) do
  collection = Collection.all.sample
  event = collection.events.sample
  create_deliveries = proc do |wh|
    Webhook::Delivery.insert_all([
      { webhook_id: wh.id, event_id: event.id, state: :completed, response: { code: 200 }, request: {} },
      { webhook_id: wh.id, event_id: event.id, state: :completed, response: { code: 422 }, request: {} },
      { webhook_id: wh.id, event_id: event.id, state: :completed, response: { error: :failed_tls }, request: {} },
      { webhook_id: wh.id, event_id: event.id, state: :errored, response: {}, request: {} },
      { webhook_id: wh.id, event_id: event.id, state: :in_progress, response: {}, request: {} },
      { webhook_id: wh.id, event_id: event.id, state: :pending, response: {}, request: {} }
    ], record_timestamps: true)
  end
  
  Webhook.create!(collection: collection, name: "Active Webhook", url: "https://example.com", subscribed_actions: %w[card_assigned card_popped comment_created]).tap { |wh| create_deliveries.(wh) }
  Webhook.create!(collection: collection, name: "Deactivated Webhook", url: "https://example.com", active: false).tap { |wh| create_deliveries.(wh) }
end
```
To deactivate a Webhook run:
```ruby
ApplicationRecord.with_tenant(<tenant>) { Webhook.find(<id>).deactivate }
```

title: Watchers
body: This is a revamp of the way people watch collections. It introduces a new UI that clearly shows who's watching for new cards and let's you toggle that for yourself with one click. No more puzzling about what the settings are or wondering if you're adding cards into the void. This also simplifies the collection access involvements to just `watching` and `access_only` and eliminates the `everything` option. The latter is confusing and almost no one actually wants the firehose. Now watching just means "watching for new cards" like the UI says. Here's how it breaks down: **Everyone is always notified about (including people not watching):** - Comments on cards you're subscribed to. - @mentions - Cards that are assigned to them . **Collection Watchers are additionally notified about:** - New cards added to the collection. To-do: - [ ] I'm not sure that passing around a param to opt out of rendering the list is the best way to do this. - [ ] We probably need to run a script on the server to convert existing `everything` subscriptions to `watching`.

title: Extract proprietary integrations into an engine
body:
Lots of structural changes in here, but nothing *functional* is changing.

ref: https://3.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/37331921/todos/9061920236

## Summary

I've created a new Rails engine `fizzy-saas`, which lives in-app at `gems/fizzy-saas` for now (we will move it into a separate repository later). Our internal gem dependencies like 37id and queenbee (and their initializers) are all moved to the engine, as are all the queenbee/launchpad-related controllers, models, and helpers.

## Details

The app can now be run in two modes:

- launchpad authentication (the default)
- local authentication (set `LOCAL_AUTHENTICATION=1`)

When running in local-auth mode, the `fizzy-saas` gem and its dependencies are not loaded (see `Gemfile` for details), so it's possible to ship an open-source version of Fizzy without it.  The tests all pass in both modes, and **must continue to do so**: so both modes are exercised by `bin/ci`.

Seeds have been updated to be runnable in either mode; but no guarantees that the seeds from one mode will work in an app running in the other mode. To be safe, if you're switching back and forth, run `bin/setup --reset`.

The engine integration is a bit non-standard because we only care about the engine running in Fizzy, not in any general application. So:

1. the engine does not have `test/dummy` and does not have an independent test suite. Instead, the Fizzy suite will run any test files present in `gems/fizzy-test` unless it's in local-auth mode. (See `bin/rails` for details.)
2. Likewise, there are hooks in `bin/setup` to do fizzy-saas-specific setup.
3. Some models and controllers are extended directly by the engine:
   ```ruby
   User.prepend User::SignalUser
   Account.prepend Account::SignalAccount
   LoginHelper.prepend LoginHelper::SignalLogin
   SessionsController.include Sessions::SignalSessions
   ```

This branch is also pinned temporarily to the Rails branch from https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/55668 so that the account slug works properly.

## Remaining work:

There are some remaining references to queenbee_id and signal_id in column names. We should rename these at some point, but they are unused in local-auth mode and so it is not critical to do so.

title: Nav filter handle collapsed sections
body:
A couple improvements to the collapsible sections in the main Fizzy nav.

1. Remember the open/closed state of nav sections after page refreshes using localStorage.
2. When filtering, temporarily open all sections so you can see the matches.
3. When not filtering, go back to the state saved in localStorage.

This release focuses on bug fixes and compatibility improvements across multiple lexers. We've fixed Ruby method definition highlighting for comparable methods. title: Columns
body:
https://3.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/37331921/messages/9098262817

We are introducing some core [domain changes here](https://3.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/37331921/todos/9104468256). Most notably, this introduces a new column model. A collection can have a list of columns, and cards can have an associated column.

title: Collection notifications fix
body:
Fixes a couple supremely confusing things with the collection notification settings page. Before, we were simply hiding the text labels for the involvement button. Unfortunately, that completely reversed the meaning of the buttons:

`🔔 Watch this` became `🔔`, which looks like you currently have notifications enabled (even though you don't).

This PR changes things so that when an involvement button has `icon_only: true`, the icon is flipped. I also ensured that the `icon_only` prop persists between turboframe reloads.

title: Bump sentry-rails from 5.27.0 to 5.28.0
body:
Bumps [sentry-rails](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-ruby) from 5.27.0 to 5.28.0.
Changelog

Sourced from sentry-rails's changelog.

5.28.0

Features

  • Auto-enable Rails structured logging when enable_logs is true (#2721)

Miscellaneous

  • Deprecate all Metrics related APIs #2726

    Sentry no longer has the Metrics Beta offering so all the following APIs linked to Metrics have been deprecated and will be removed in the next major.

    Sentry.init do |config|
  # ...
  config.metrics.enabled = true
  config.metrics.enable_code_locations = true
  config.metrics.before_emit = lambda {}
end

    Sentry::Metrics.increment('button_click')
    
Sentry::Metrics.distribution('page_load', 15.0, unit: 'millisecond')
    
Sentry::Metrics.gauge('page_load', 15.0, unit: 'millisecond')
    
Sentry::Metrics.set('user_view', 'jane')
    
Sentry::Metrics.timing('how_long') { sleep(1) }

Internal

  • Fix leftover config.logger call in graphql patch (#2722
  • Add Configuration.before and Configuration.after to run hooks before and after given event (#2724)

5.27.1

Features

  • Support for :origin attribute in log events (#2712)

Bug Fixes

  • Skip including sentry.message.template in the log event attributes if there are no interpolation parameters provided (#2700)
  • Respect log_level when logging via :std_lib_logger patch (#2709)
  • Add sentry.origin attribute to log events (#2712)

Populate writer and last transaction in responses
body:
In order to control routing dynamically, we need to expose some Beamer information to the proxy.

The `beamer_writer` value is used by the proxy to keep track of which node should receive write requests. When it changes due to a failover, the proxy will update after seeing a new value in this header. We provide this to the proxy in the `X-Writer` response header.

The `beamer_last_txn` value will be used to control writer pinning. Setting it in the cookie here is the first stage of this. The second stage will be to catch situations where a reader gets a request where this header value is set to a large value than the reader has seen; when that happens if means there's a risk of reading stale data, so rather than serve the request we should request the proxy to reproxy it back to the writer.

We also set `X-Kamal-Target` in the response to match the `X-Kamal-Target` that was set in the request; this lets us see which proxy target served each request, which is useful for diagnostics.

(This is likely to evolve a bit when we move onto the Beamer gem.)

title: Mobile columns
body:
This properly scrolls columns along the x-axis when it doesn't all fit on the screen.

It was rather a trick to figure out how to get scrolling to work on small viewports while still centering content on large viewports. We can't use `justify-content: center` on the column grid container because it keeps you from scrolling to left overflow content. Instead, columns are now `justify-content: start` (which allows scrolling to work properly) and we use `margin-inline: auto` to make sure content sits in the center of the screen.

This is **Step 1** of getting columns to work well on smaller viewports. It handles any case where the column content doesn't fit, regardless of the screen size. **Step 2** will involve more deliberate mobile styles that take place at a mobile breakpoint.

Smoother expand transitions for columns
body:
Nicer transitions for columns. Here's what changed:

1. Set cards to a fixed width to prevent layout shift while transitioning. Before, cards were really narrow during the transition which triggered layout reflow on each card (i.e. it was expensive to render).
2. Add a wrapper around the cards with `overflow: hidden`. This wrapper adapts to the size of the column and crops the cards during transition. Had to add a bit of padding so card shadows aren't cropped.
3. Add `transition-property`. We weren't setting this before, which meant every property was being transitioned (expensive!)
4. Use simpler rules for the column width. Before, we were using a combination of `flex`, `inline-size`, `max-inline-size`, and `min-inline-size`. There might have been a good reason for that (let me know if I'm missing something, @jzimdars), but removing all this in favor of `inline-size` seems to work well and simplifies things. It also prevents an annoying layout shift where the width of all columns was slightly smaller during a transition.

title: pre-connect: make sure we're matching against unquoted hostnames

dev: Fix the default tenant to be the correct Honcho id
Fix crash during migrations audit
body:
I've ran into an issue where this audit always fails.

```
Database: Check migrations
bin/migration-audit


Migration or schema files changed:
db/migrate/20251015081645_create_account_join_codes.rb
db/schema.rb
db/schema_cache.yml

▸ Deleting schema files
rm -f db/schema.rb db/schema_cache.yml

▸ Deleting tenant directory
rm -rf storage/tenants/development/175932900

▸ Regenerating schema files
bin/rails db:migrate

fatal: ambiguous argument 'db/schema.rb': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.
Use '--' to separate paths from revisions, like this:
'git <command> [<revision>...] -- [<file>...]'

✗ Schema files are out of sync with migrations!

Differences:
fatal: ambiguous argument 'db/schema.rb': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.
Use '--' to separate paths from revisions, like this:
'git <command> [<revision>...] -- [<file>...]'
```

The problem was that I'm missing tenant 175932900, so deleting the dir wouldn't cause migrations to re-run, and would leave me with a missing schema.rb file (because the audit deletes it).
This would then lead to a crash because git diff gets passe a non-existent file.

This PR, switches the logic around such that the schema gets deleted and then a new tenant gets created, this then runs all tenanted migrations. After the migrations run, the new tenant's database gets deleted.

title: Ensure check icons are targeted properly
body:
We have a couple different ways of showing ✔︎ icons for `popup__item`. Quick filters use `[aria-selected]`, and the Accounts section in the main nav uses `popup__item--current`. This was causing specificity conflicts.

This PR consolidates this behavior into the popup CSS file. Now all ✔︎ icons are hidden unless the item has the `aria-checked` attribute.

title: Bump sentry-rails from 5.28.0 to 6.0.0
body:
Bumps [sentry-rails](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-ruby) from 5.28.0 to 6.0.0.
Changelog

Sourced from sentry-rails's changelog.

6.0.0

Breaking Changes

  • Drop support for rubies below 2.7 #2743
    • Drop support for Rails below 5.2.0
    • Drop support for Sidekiq below 5.0
  • Remove deprecated config.async #1894
  • Remove deprecated Sentry::Metrics and config.metrics and all metrics related code (#2729)
  • Remove deprecated config.capture_exception_frame_locals, use include_local_variables instead (#2730)
  • Remove deprecated config.enable_tracing, use config.traces_sample_rate = 1.0 instead (#2731)
  • Remove deprecated config.logger=, use config.sdk_logger= instead (#2732)
  • Sentry.logger now always points to the StructuredLogger (#2752)
  • Remove deprecated Sentry::Rails::Tracing::ActionControllerSubscriber (#2733)
  • Remove deprecated Event#configuration (#2740)
  • Remove deprecated Sentry::Client#generate_sentry_trace and Sentry::Client#generate_baggage (#2741)
  • Remove Transaction deprecations (#2736)
    • Remove deprecated constant Sentry::Transaction::SENTRY_TRACE_REGEXP, use Sentry::PropagationContext::SENTRY_TRACE_REGEXP instead
    • Remove deprecated method Sentry::Transaction.from_sentry_trace, use Sentry.continue_trace instead
    • Remove deprecated method Sentry::Transaction.extract_sentry_trace, use Sentry::PropagationContext.extract_sentry_trace instead
    • Remove deprecated attribute Sentry::Transaction.configuration
    • Remove deprecated attribute Sentry::Transaction.hub
    • Remove deprecated argument hub to Sentry::Transaction.finish
    • Remove deprecated argument hub to Sentry::Transaction#initialize (#2739)
  • Remove :monotonic_active_support_logger from config.breadcrumbs_logger (#2717)
  • Migrate from to_hash to to_h (#2351)
  • Add before_send_check_in for applying to CheckInEvent (#2703)
  • Returning a hash from before_send and before_send_transaction is no longer supported and will drop the event.
  • config.enabled_environments now defaults to nil instead of [] for sending to all environments (#2716)
  • Requests which have response status codes in the inclusive ranges [(301..303), (305..399), (401..404)] will no longer create transactions by default. See config.trace_ignore_status_codes below to control what gets traced.
  • Stacktrace truncation for oversized events now takes 500 frames on each side instead of 250.

Features

  • Add config.trace_ignore_status_codes to control which response codes to ignore for tracing (#2725)

    You can pass in an Array of individual status codes or ranges of status codes.

    Sentry.init do |config|
    # ...
    # will ignore 404, 501, 502, 503
    config.trace_ignore_status_codes = [404, (501..503)]
end

  • Add config.profiles_sample_interval to control sampling frequency (#2745)

    • Both stackprof and vernier now get sampled at a default frequency of 101 Hz.

  • Request body reading checks for :rewind to match Rack 3 behavior. (#2754)

title: Group notifications by card and only show the oldest one in the tray
body:
https://app.box-car.com/5986089/cards/1328

This adds support for grouping notifications by card id in the notifications tray, so that it only show the oldest one. 

This uses a stimulus controller versus server-side handling due to:

- This works dynamically with new notifications that show up. They will be grouped as expected dynamically.
- Unifying notifications by card ID with a query is complex, since there can be many sources for a notification with different ways of fetching the card depending on the kind.

Styling is pending. This adds two elements to play with the styles:

- A class that is adedd to grouped notifications.
- A counter with the grouped notifications that is updated dynamically.

Pending:

- [x] Design

title: Sticky columns
body:
Add column titles when dragging over columns, especially useful when you're scrolled down the page and the column names aren't visible. Also uses the column colors to flavor the drag-and-drop outline.

CSS has some interesting limits we're running into ([more details here](https://app.fizzy.do/5986089/cards/2781)):

- Column children can't use `position: sticky` if we want to be able to scroll horizontally on small screens.
- Column children can't use `position: fixed` if we want to maintain smooth column transitions.

To get around this, I added column wrappers which don't have transforms (which means we can use fixed position titles). Fixed position is an important piece here so the title is always visible within the viewport, even if you have 100 cards and are scrolled really far down.

It's admittedly a bit redundant to have the titles show up when the headers are already visible on the screen. We'll need to add some JS if we want to only show when you're scrolled down.

title: Fix aggressive cacheing rule on session menu
body:
Fixes https://app.fizzy.do/6074589/cards/5

This is a tricky caching situation. The Account is in a tenanted DB, and the Membership is untenanted, so I can't touch the membership when the account updates. This leaves me with 3 options:
1. Move the Account, or at least its name, to the untenanted part of the app
    This doesn't feel right, but would work. Updating the account name makes a post to the untenanted part, this changes the name and touches all associated memberships, the cache busts and everything works. Though now we have tenant data in the untenanted part of the app :/
2. Do an N+1 to fetch the all accounts updated_at timestamp and add that to the cache key
    This would also work, though we'd have read the memberships from the DB and all their accounts. So this becomes a diminishing return as caching would only skip rendering part of the view.
3. Disable caching all together

I ruled out 1 as a realistic option and focused on 2 & 3. And after some benchmarking I got the following results:
1. Using the current caching mechanism with the bug: Median response time is 21ms
2. Adding the updated_at timestamp of the last updated account (option 2): Median response time is 28ms
3. Removing the cache completely (option 3): Median response time is 25ms

Options 2 and 3 are within a margin of error, so I opted to go with the simpler solution of removing the cache.

To somewhat improve the situation, I also updated the dialog controller to fix `loading=lazy` behavior of Turbo Frames.
The fix triggers the turbo frame's observer when the dialog is shown, this usually doesn't happen.

Somewhat related, I noticed I didn't add pagination on the menu, so I went to check how slow that would be in extreme cases where someone has say 100 accounts, and it's really slow - around 700ms.

title: Sticky column headers using fixed
body:
Adds column titles during drag and drop.

- If the expander button is off screen, we add a class that we can use in CSS to…
- Add an `::after` pseudo-element with the column title on hover, using `position: fixed` so it's always at the top of the screen.
- Since `position: fixed` doesn't work when an ancestor has a `transform` applied, I moved all the transition effects to a new wrapper inside the column. That way the column itself allows for its hover title to be fixed, but all the transition stuff still works nicely.

Related: [Remove text-matching @mentions?](https://app.fizzy.do/5986089/cards/2874/)

Changing the plain text representation to first name + initial in last name fixed it: `Good job @fernandoo`.

title: MySQL search
body:
Add 16 search_index table (search_index_0 .. search_index_15) for full-text search of cards and comments. The records are sharded across the tables by account_id. This is for performance as MySQL cannot pre-filter fulltext search results. Each fulltext index requires 11 internal tables so this creates 192 tables in total (see https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/innodb-fulltext-index.html).

For the search there is a full-text index on the title and content columns. The board_ids is also included in the table and accessible board ids are pre-loaded and included in the search query. This allows us to filter out inaccessible records before joining with other tables.

Right now the search is just using boolean search. This would give us a bunch of syntax options
(see https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/fulltext-boolean.html) except the search query filters those out.

I've removed the searchable_by method for now - everything is built on the assumption that there's a single search index table and all data must fit into it.

Queries are written in SQL, we don't have a SearchIndex models. The sharding and custom query language mean it would be a light wrapper for raw SQL anyway. 

Queries and documents are pre-processed to replace words with their stemmed version. Highlighting and snippeting is done in Ruby on the results from the database.

Data can be reindexed with the search:reindex rake task.

We'll also run jobs on every app server for the moment, until we split them out to separate instances.

title: Use uuid as the id type in schema.rb
body:
This matches the format in the migration files and makes the type_to_sql override redundant.

The only wart we are left with is that since there are no true UUID types in MySQL we'll have to assume that binary(16) columns are UUIDs.

In practice this is probably fine as the MySQL adapter doesn't map any other types to binary.

title: Finish adding account_id to tables and models
body:
Schema:
- add account_id to tables it was missing from
- make account_id a required column everywhere
- add [account_id] indexes, or add `account_id` to existing indices

Models:
- add `belongs_to :account` to all models (default to using a domain
  model's account whenever possible)
- add account_id in all the necessary fixtures
- add account_id to insert_all hashes
- pass account_id to a few initialize calls

Note that I'm not adding account_id to the join tables primarily
because I couldn't think of an easy way to populate it without making

title: Replace Search::Index with Search::Records
body:
Lean on ActiveRecord models for searching and strip out the raw SQL. Replaces the `search_index_*` tables with sharded `search_records_*` tables as that allows us to use a Search::Record model name.

A Class is dynamically created for each record table shard so that we and we can access it via the `Search::Record.for_account(account_id)` method.

title: Stalled cards are unstalled by anything that touches updated_at
body:
This implementation also compares `updated_at` against `STALLED_AFTER_LAST_SPIKE_PERIOD`, so that a possible timeline would be:

- card is published
- card has an activity spike
- time passes, card becomes stalled
- card is touched, and becomes unstalled
- time passes, card becomes stalled again

Currently the "time passes" value is 14 days (`Card::Stallable::STALLED_AFTER_LAST_SPIKE_PERIOD`) for both post-activity-spike and post-touch time comparisons.

An alternative implementation could be to remove the activity spike when a stalled card is touched; if we did that then the card would not stall again until there is first another activity spike. In this implementation, the card will re-stall every two weeks.

ref: https://app.fizzy.do/5986089/cards/2492

title: Add optimistic pausing to avoid steal reads
body:
Instead of writer pinning, we'll track the last transaction ID of each write. Then on each read we'll check whether the replica already contains this transaction. If it doesn't, there's a chance of a stale read, so we'll briefly wait for it to catch up. If it doesn't catch up quickly enough, just bail and accept the possibility of the read being stale.

The theory being, often after a write the replication logs and the subsequent read requests will be racing each other to get to the new data, but commonly the replication gets there first. And even if a subsequent read request does get there first, the replication data will arrive very shortly after.

If in fact we see that, in practice, requests do commonly have to wait for the replicated data, we could move the delay out to the proxy layer by having it re-proxy the request after a short wait. That could free up Puma to serve another request sooner. But this way is very simple to try, so let's see how it behaves first.

**Still validating this idea!** I'd like to kick this a bit harder on staging and see if it's worth doing, and also see whether offloading those sleeps to the proxy is worth the complexity. First impressions: when I try this, I'm getting 100% of my reads from the local DC, and no delay is being applied. (So it either works great, or is broken :rofl:)

This should fix the recurring ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError errors from ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob.

The issue is that, when images are not direct uploaded (e.g. a card background image or avatar image), the AnalyzeJob has been getting enqueued before the file itself was uploaded to blob storage.

Setting ActiveJob::Base.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true makes sure that jobs are always enqueued only once *all* transactions have been committed.

This will be the Rails default at some point, but for now we still need to explicitly set it.

title: Prevent overlapping bundles from being created
body:
ref: https://3.basecamp.com/2914079/buckets/27/card_tables/cards/9275047474

The recurring issue with overlapping notification bundles was due to notifications being handled out-of-order. The test added here is illustrative, but to save you a click:

```ruby
first_notification = @user.notifications.create!(source: events(:logo_published), creator: @user)
second_notification = @user.notifications.create!(source: events(:logo_published), creator: @user)
assert first_notification.created_at < second_notification.created_at

# process in reverse chronological order
@user.bundle(second_notification)
@user.bundle(first_notification)

assert_equal 1, @user.notification_bundles.pending.count # FAIL, there are 2
```

I imagine this order of events could happen by pure chance. But two small bugs coincide to result in overlapping bundles:

1. Bundle creation relies on `set_default_window` to set `ends_at`, but `set_default_window` was being called _after_ validation, and so `validate_no_overlapping` wasn't working properly for new records.
2. `User::Notifiable#find_or_create_bundle_for` does not handle the case where the notification's timestamp is before the current pending bundle.

So the two fixes applied are:

- call `Bundle#set_default_window` before validation (but only for new records)
- in `User::Notifiable#find_or_create_bundle_for`, expand the window on the existing current bundle to include the notification, if the notification pre-dates the bundle

cc @jorgemanrubia

title: Open source / SaaS split
body:
Separate SaaS and open source versions of Fizzy.

The default version will be the open source one, that runs on SQLite. This is built on top of the work by @djmb in https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/pull/1669. @flavorjones had done some previous work where the semantics was inverted (opt-in into open source). I think it makes more sense to have the vanilla open source version as the default, now that we are going to make the whole thing public.

This PR introduces a mehanism to enable the SAAS version of the app:

1. Setting an env var `SAAS=1` (this will enable the private gems and configure the MySQL adapter).
2. Having a file `tmp/saas.txt`. There are rake tasks to touch/remove it `bin/rails saas:enable` and `bin/rails saas:disable`. 

(2) is meant for our own dev work, so that don't have to worry about passing the env var during regular daily work. The goal here is having good development ergonomics for everyone:

- Open source users clone the repo and have it ready to go with Sqlite.
- We at 37signals clone the repo, touch `tmp/saas.txt` and we are ready to go with our private extensions and MySQL, using exactly the same scripts vanilla users would use.

For configuring the private gems, this introduces a separated `Gemfile.saas` file, that includes the original `Gemfile` and adds the private gems. In SaaS mode, it will configure the bundle file automaticalyl to use the saas one.

(1) is meant to be set in our SaaS hosts via our SaaS Dockerfile, although obviously you are free to use that too locally.

This also moves several bits to the [`fizzy-saas` gem, which now lives in its own private repo](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy-saas):

- Database configuration. This extracts two vanilla adapters in the open source version `database.mysql.yml` and `database.sqlite.yml` and, in SaaS mode, uses the `database.yml` from the gem. This way, we can keep our very specific MySQL setup outside of the open source version.
- Kamal deploy configuration and hooks.
- Fragments of `bin/setup` that are specific to 37signals.

Pending:

- [x]  Move our Dockerfile to the gem too. Set SAAS env var in Docker.
- [x] Move secrets to the gem. We need to extend kamal to let you configure the path for secrets in the deploy descriptor.
- [x] Leave vanilla Kamal setup in the gem.
- [x] SaaS tests passing (2 failing)
- [x] QA in staging / beta

title: Check and report on Sec-Fetch-Site header for forgery protection
body:
This is a great, solid alternative to CSRF tokens for CSRF protection when we aren't worried about older browsers or other kind of actors doing modifying requests in our app, and could be a good test for future upstreaming to Rails (although there we'd need to continue using CSRF tokens or at least letting people opt out manually).

Let's start checking the header and reporting on it when CSRF fails or when it doesn't match the other checks Rails does, and then promote this to be the only way to defend from CSRF.

More about Sec-Fetch-Site header [here](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Sec-Fetch-Site), and about how this can be used to defend from CSRF [here](https://www.alexedwards.net/blog/preventing-csrf-in-go).

body:
- Adds a button in Account Settings where you can request a ZIP export of your Fizzy data
- Export files are created in the background. When ready, a link to download them is sent to the requester.
- Exports expire after 24 hours. They are limited to 10 per day.

Follow-up work that isn't part of this PR:
- If you exceed the limit of export requests we should indicate that in the UI. Currently there's no indication of why you can't request more exports, it just won't let you do it.
- The export job isn't resumable yet. We could improve on this by having it stash the files that it's processed so far into the export's attachment, and then download it to continue working when it resumes.

title: Menu header collapsing on it's own
body:
**The issue**
When using the shortcut, or clicking the menu at the top, the menu will close itself in < 1 second. This means I can't read the contents of the menu before tapping the shortcut or confirming the shortcut with the Return key.

**Implications**
This makes fizzy.do unusable. 

**Expected behavior**
I expect the menu to stay open until I hit Esc or click off of it. 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a5ff246-42cb-4196-a57b-3fd1de45d297)


**Mitigation**
Logging out and back in seemed to resolve the problem, until I tapped: J (for menu), 2 (for assigned to me) and Return (to confirm the selection).

title: Robots, begone
body:
* robots.txt: "Please, don't come in." If a page is directly linked, the URL can still appear in search results, though.
* X-Robots-Tag: "If you're here, forget what you saw." Works even if the crawler ignores robots.txt or reaches a page via external link. Can remove already-indexed pages.
* Public boards may be indexed. They're meant to be shareable and discoverable, not just private link sharing.

title: Fix `bin/setup` to explicitly use bash syntax for `mise hook-env`
body:
The bin/setup script fails when a user's default shell is Fish, producing this error:

```
bin/setup: line 88: set: -g: invalid option
set: usage: set [--abefhkmnptuvxBCHP] [-o option] [arg ...]
```

This PR explicitly tells mise to output bash-compatible syntax by adding the `-s` bash flag

This ensures the script works correctly regardless of the user's default shell configuration.

title: Allow typing magic links on mobile

When typing a magic link, rather than pasting it, iOS seems to send `keydown.enter`, and we weren't submitting the form in that case.

Changed to submit the form in either case (paste or enter), and use the state of the input target to help guard against double submissions.

title: Don't navigate if a dialog is open within the navigable list

We need to ignore navigation if an edit dialog is open within the navigable list. Right now if you open the Edit dialog and hit the left/right arrows within the text input, card navigation still happens even though you'd expect focus to be within the input.

Here, I'm adding a Stimulus target to each dialog that should pause navigation. This works well enough, but it would be nice to return focus once the dialog closes.

cc @jorgemanrubia

title: Add console1984 and audits1984 for access logs and auditing
body:
A couple of decisions I'd love feedback on before merging and deploying this:

1. For OSS users, new secrets have to be generated for prod envs even if they aren't interested in audit functionality.

   Fizzy could fall back to dummy keys if they're not set, but that seems like a security problem waiting to happen. If users don't care about it, I think they can pretty easily inject dummy values themselves. It's mildly annoying, but better than unintentionally using known secrets in production.

title: Warn users when mise is not activated
body:
## Summary

I'm not sure if this is needed but I needed this to overcome a Ruby/bundler setup issue by:

1. **Adding Ruby to `.mise.toml`**: Explicitly configures mise to manage Ruby 3.4.7 installation. Without this, mise may skip installing Ruby if a system Ruby exists (I had system ruby installed via pacman), causing gem executables (like `bundle`) to be installed in locations outside of mise's PATH management.

```
fizzy main ❯ ./bin/setup

   ˚ ∘             ∘ ˚
  ∘˚˳°∘°  𝒻𝒾𝓏𝓏𝓎  °∘°˳˚∘

▸ Installing Ruby
mise install --yes
mise all tools are installed

./bin/setup: line 124: bundle: command not found
```

2. **Warning about mise activation**: Adds a check in `bin/setup` to warn users if mise is not activated in their shell configuration. Without this, `ruby` and `bundle` won't be available after setup completes. I didn't have mise installed before this and didn't have activate in my rc files.

## What I think was happening

The project has a `.ruby-version` file, but it didn't seem like  mise was detecting/installing Ruby from it. When system Ruby matched the version, mise would skip installation, causing gems to install to user directories outside of mise's managed PATH.

Might be a doc or a user error and not a patch. This is just what I needed to do.

title: Add Missing Production Databases for Solid Queue and Solid Cache
body:
The app failed to boot on Fly.io because Rails 8 expected separate `queue` and `cache` databases in production, but the MySQL config only defined `primary` and `cable`.

## Root Cause

Rails 8 uses Solid Queue and Solid Cache in production, and both require their own database connections. The MySQL config didn’t include `queue` or `cache` entries for the production environment.

## Fix

Added `queue` and `cache` database definitions to `config/database.mysql.yml` under `production`, matching the existing SQLite setup.

### Production databases now include:

* `fizzy_production`
* `fizzy_production_cable`
* `fizzy_production_queue`
* `fizzy_production_cache`

Development and test remain unchanged because they don’t use database-backed queue/cache.

title: Immediate avatar and embed variants
body:
Process variants synchronously on attachment to close the window between image upload and variant availability, guaranteeing that we won't have lazy variant processing attempts in GET requests.

Tradeoff is that we do variant processing in upload requests, which is actually desirable. We're working with images that should take milliseconds to resize given that we'll already have the file on hand.

Note there's a tricky gotcha with when after-commit hooks fire since they're per connection pool. This leads to variant processing occurring at different times for SaaS/non-SaaS due to the replica connection! Hence the change to explicitly create Blobs before attaching them, guaranteeing predictable ordering.

References https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/51951

/cc @flavorjones @dhh @tomrossi7

title: Mark users as "verified" and only send notifications to verified users
body:
## Motivation

Today, spammers can add users to an account by consuming join codes; and those users will receive notification emails even if they never log in to confirm their identity. This enables spam delivery via notification emails, which we need to prevent.

## Details

Add a verified_at timestamp to users that is set when they reedem a join link, by inserting a verification step into two flows:

1. if they are already logged in with the identity that matches the email provided during join link redemption:
   - redeem a join link → **verify** → user join form
2. otherwise:
   - redeem a join link → submit a valid magic link code → **verify** → user join form

The "verify" step above is implemented with a new controller, `Users::VerificationsController`.

The `JoinCodesController` will redirect the user to `new_users_verification_url` either directly or via `session[:return_to_after_authenticating]` and the `Sesssions::MagicLinkController`. The `VerificationsController` uses an auto-submit form so that a redirect can be converted into a POST action and write to the database.

Two notes:
- Account owners are auto-verified on creation.
- Backfilling "verified" status is nontrivial. A backfill script marks existing users as verified based on evidence of real activity (created cards, comments, reactions, etc.).

Finally, Fizzy will only send notification emails to users who have verified their email address.

## Rollout

Ideally this would get rolled out in three steps:

1. roll out the database migrations and code to set `verified_at`
2. run the backfill script
3. roll out enforcement of verification when emailing notifications

but we could do it all at once if we're careful not to overlap the process with invocation of the recurring job `deliver_bundled_notifications`.

Using the card or comment `updated_at` is fraught because we do so much touching of records (e.g., comment is touched when a reaction is added; card is touched when a comment is added). Let's display the search record's `created_at`, which is the ordering used for the overall results: https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/blob/642506e79ed5a0a4e977d1e3ea099c48b1ae0aaf/app/models/search/record.rb#L35-L42

title: Update event.json.jbuilder
body:
## What this does
This PR updates the webhook JSON payload to include more useful information for integrations (like n8n or Zapier).

Specifically, it adds:
- **Card Description:** The rich text content of the card.
- **Assignees:** A list of user names assigned to the card.
- **Comments:** A full history of comments on the card (including user, plain text, and HTML).

## Why
Currently, the webhook sends metadata but misses the actual content of the card/comment. This makes it difficult to build automations that react to what users are actually saying or doing inside the card.

## Note to Maintainers
I am a "low-code" contributor and do not have a local Rails environment set up to test this. 

I wrote this code by following the patterns I saw in `_card.json.jbuilder` and `_comment.json.jbuilder`. I would appreciate it if you could verify that the syntax is correct and that it passes your test suite. Thanks!

title: Adopt a cooldown period for dependency updates
body:
As suggested by @flavorjones, with more background in [this article](https://blog.yossarian.net/2025/11/21/We-should-all-be-using-dependency-cooldowns). 

This applies:
- 7 days as default: from the article, a 7-day cooldown would have prevented 8 out of 10 recent supply chain attacks. It seems reasonably long but not crazy long.
- 14 days for major versions, to give some time to the community to find problems.

For some dependencies (e.g. Rails), we target edge, but we don't rely on Dependabot for these; we update them manually.

title: Fix ActiveStorage FileNotFoundError with immediate variant processing
body:
When ActiveStorage::Record uses `connects_to` for read replica support, it creates a separate connection pool from ApplicationRecord. This causes `after_commit` callbacks to fire in non-deterministic order - the Attachment's `create_variants` callback can fire before the User model's upload callback completes, resulting in FileNotFoundError.

The fix removes replica connection configuration from ActiveStorage::Record so it shares the same connection pool as application models, ensuring proper callback ordering.

Also reverts test workarounds that were added to work around this issue, since the root cause is now fixed.

See: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/53694

/cc @basecamp/sip @jorgemanrubia

title: Stream response in webhook request manually to check size
body:
This addresses a DoS vulnerability where the response might be massive, leading to OOM errors, as the response is read in full in memory by default.

To prevent this, we need to read the body in chunks, checking the size of the chunks we've read and raising if we go over a certain limit.

I've set the limit to 100 KB because the responses to these requests should be fairly small or even empty, and we only care about the status code in the end.

title: Add env-configurable option to disable public signups
body:
This PR adds a simple single-tenant (“no public signup”) mode controlled by the `SINGLE_TENANT` environment variable.

When `SINGLE_TENANT=true `and at least one user already exists(similarly to once-campfire):
- /signup/new redirects to the login page instead of showing the signup form.
- /session/new no longer allows creating new accounts.

To avoid exposing whether an email exists, the page always displays the generic message:
“Check your inbox if your email belongs to an existing account.”


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/195c33f0-c179-4938-b8af-b97b2fe40ab3

title: API: Support `created_at` for API card and comment creation
body:
As discussed in https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/pull/1766#issuecomment-3637846074, this adds the ability to import cards and comments with their original timestamps.

### What
- Accept `created_at` when creating cards via the API.  
- Accept `created_at` when creating comments.  
- Avoid overwriting a provided `created_at` during initial publication.  
- Update API docs accordingly.

### Why
Needed for importing historical items, such as GitHub issues and their comments, while keeping accurate timelines.

### Notes
- `created_at` is optional. Existing behavior is unchanged when omitted.
- UI flows stay the same.

### Example
```json
{
  "card": {
    "title": "Imported issue",
    "created_at": "2023-05-14T10:23:45Z"
  }
}

title: API: fix direct upload with bearer token
body:
Adds a new API endpoint for direct uploads that works with bearer token authentication.

The existing `/rails/active_storage/direct_uploads` endpoint doesn't work with API bearer tokens because `ActiveStorage::DirectUploadsController` inherits from `ActiveStorage::BaseController` (not `ApplicationController`), so it doesn't get Fizzy's CSRF bypass for JSON requests or the bearer token authentication (See also efbd2cc3d).

This PR adds `Api::DirectUploadsController` which:
- Inherits from `ApplicationController` (gets bearer auth + account context automatically)
- Sets the required ActiveStorage URL options for generating upload URLs
- Returns `attachable_sgid` (required for ActionText) in addition to `signed_id`

Follow-up to #1766.

## Use case

I'm building a script to import GitHub issues into Fizzy. GitHub issues contain images hosted on `github.com/user-attachments/...` which require authentication to download. The import script:

1. Downloads images from GitHub using `gh api`
2. Uploads them to Fizzy via this new direct upload endpoint
3. Embeds them in card descriptions using `<action-text-attachment sgid="...">`

Without this endpoint, there's no way to upload files via the API.

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer your-token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"blob":{"filename":"image.png","byte_size":12345,"checksum":"...","content_type":"image/png"}}' \
  https://app.fizzy.do/123456789/api/direct_uploads.json
```

See also https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/discussions/2054

title: Fix direct uploads via API
body:
Closes: https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/discussions/2054 Test script: ```bash #!/bin/bash # Configuration API_TOKEN="5y5yT2QGxYrM6FJbZwrTxnCB" BASE_URL="http://fizzy.localhost:3006/897362094" CARD_ID="4" FILE_PATH="test/fixtures/files/moon.jpg" # Get file info FILENAME=$(basename "$FILE_PATH") BYTE_SIZE=$(stat -c%s "$FILE_PATH") CONTENT_TYPE="image/jpeg" CHECKSUM=$(openssl dgst -md5 -binary "$FILE_PATH" | openssl base64) echo "Uploading: $FILENAME ($BYTE_SIZE bytes)" echo "Checksum: $CHECKSUM" echo "" # Step 1: Create direct upload echo "Step 1: Creating direct upload..." DIRECT_UPLOAD_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "$BASE_URL/rails/active_storage/direct_uploads" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{ \"blob\": { \"filename\": \"$FILENAME\", \"byte_size\": $BYTE_SIZE, \"checksum\": \"$CHECKSUM\", \"content_type\": \"$CONTENT_TYPE\" } }") echo "Response: $DIRECT_UPLOAD_RESPONSE" echo "" # Extract upload URL and signed_id UPLOAD_URL=$(echo "$DIRECT_UPLOAD_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.direct_upload.url') SIGNED_ID=$(echo "$DIRECT_UPLOAD_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.signed_id') if [ "$UPLOAD_URL" = "null" ] || [ -z "$UPLOAD_URL" ]; then echo "Error: Failed to get upload URL" exit 1 fi echo "Upload URL: $UPLOAD_URL" echo "Signed ID: $SIGNED_ID" echo "" read -p "Press Enter to continue to Step 2..." echo "" # Step 2: Upload file to the direct upload URL # Extract all required headers from the response UPLOAD_CONTENT_TYPE=$(echo "$DIRECT_UPLOAD_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.direct_upload.headers["Content-Type"]') UPLOAD_CONTENT_MD5=$(echo "$DIRECT_UPLOAD_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.direct_upload.headers["Content-MD5"]') UPLOAD_CONTENT_DISPOSITION=$(echo "$DIRECT_UPLOAD_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.direct_upload.headers["Content-Disposition"]') echo "Step 2: Uploading file..." echo "Headers: Content-Type=$UPLOAD_CONTENT_TYPE, Content-MD5=$UPLOAD_CONTENT_MD5" UPLOAD_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X PUT "$UPLOAD_URL" \ -H "Content-Type: $UPLOAD_CONTENT_TYPE" \ -H "Content-MD5: $UPLOAD_CONTENT_MD5" \ -H "Content-Disposition: $UPLOAD_CONTENT_DISPOSITION" \ --data-binary "@$FILE_PATH" \ -w "\nHTTP Status: %{http_code}") echo "Upload response: $UPLOAD_RESPONSE" echo "" read -p "Press Enter to continue to Step 3..." echo "" # Step 3: Attach the blob to the card via description # Extract the attachable_sgid for use in action-text-attachment ATTACHABLE_SGID=$(echo "$DIRECT_UPLOAD_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.attachable_sgid') echo "Step 3: Attaching to card description..." echo "Attachable SGID: $ATTACHABLE_SGID" ATTACH_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X PUT "$BASE_URL/cards/$CARD_ID" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{ \"card\": { \"description\": \"

Here is an image:

\" } }" \ -w "\nHTTP Status: %{http_code}") echo "Attach response: $ATTACH_RESPONSE" echo "" echo "Done!" ```

title: Refactor: Use Rails range syntax in ActivitySpike query
body:
Replace SQL string syntax with Rails range syntax for date filtering in the ActivitySpike::Detector. This improves code readability and follows Rails idioms.

Changed from:
 ```ruby 
  .where("created_at >= ?", recent_period.seconds.ago)
```

To:
```ruby
  .where(created_at: recent_period.seconds.ago..)
```

This modernizes the codebase while maintaining the same functionality.

title: Add `DSIABLE_SSL` env option
body:
`assume_ssl` and `force_ssl` are often used together:

- When running behind a terminating proxy (including Thruster) you'll want both.
- When running without SSL (like on localhost) you'll want neither.

To simplify setup for those cases, we add the `DISABLE_SSL` option. When set to `true` all SSL-related behaviour is turned off. When left as the default, it's on. This is handy for self-hosting with the Docker image, as it's one less ENV var to have to set.

We can still use `ASSUME_SSL` and `FORCE_SSL` to set those separately if required.

cc @lewispb

Refactor: use idiomatic .last instead of .order(:desc).first
body:
Simplifies the last_event method in ActivitySpike::Detector by using the more idiomatic Rails pattern .order(:created_at).last instead of .order(created_at: :desc).first. Both generate the same SQL query but .last is more readable and conventional in Rails codebases.

```ruby
fizzy(dev):002> Card.last.events.order(:created_at).last
  CACHE Card Load (0.1ms)  SELECT "cards".* FROM "cards" ORDER BY "cards"."id" DESC LIMIT ?  [["LIMIT", 1]]
  Event Load (1.0ms)  SELECT "events".* FROM "events" WHERE "events"."eventable_id" = ? AND "events"."eventable_type" = ? ORDER BY "events"."created_at" DESC LIMIT ?  [["eventable_id", "<16 bytes of binary data>"], ["eventable_type", "Card"], ["LIMIT", 1]]
```

```ruby
fizzy(dev):001> Card.last.events.order(created_at: :desc).first
  Card Load (0.3ms)  SELECT "cards".* FROM "cards" ORDER BY "cards"."id" DESC LIMIT ?  [["LIMIT", 1]]
  Event Load (0.8ms)  SELECT "events".* FROM "events" WHERE "events"."eventable_id" = ? AND "events"."eventable_type" = ? ORDER BY "events"."created_at" DESC LIMIT ?  [["eventable_id", "<16 bytes of binary data>"], ["eventable_type", "Card"], ["LIMIT", 1]]
```

title: Bundle drift detection and correction
body:
Gemfile.saas evals Gemfile, so shared gems should have identical versions in both lockfiles. This adds bin/bundle-drift to detect and fix drift:

* `bin/bundle-drift check` compares shared gem versions
* `bin/bundle-drift correct` seeds Gemfile.lock from Gemfile.saas.lock and re-locks, letting Bundler prune SaaS-only gems while preserving shared versions

Adds drift check to bin/ci and GitHub CI. Corrects existing drift.
